title: Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony
titleFull: Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (수문장 교대의식)
overview: In the Joseon dynasty, the royal guards of the palace were gatekeepers who were responsible for guarding the the main gates of Gyeongbokgung Palace as well as the main gates of the city such as Heunginjimun Gate and Sungnyemun Gate. The royal guards worked in shift duties and were in charge of opening and closing Gwanghwamun Gate. Before the royal guard system was enforced in 1469, the palace gates were protected by soldiers of the central army. The Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony held at Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Gwanghwamun area reenacts the guard-changing procedure that took place during the Joseon dynasty, along with the reproduction of costumes and weapons, based on historical records.
place: Gyeongbokgung Palace Heungnyemun Gate and Gwanghwamun Gate areas

The festival’s diverse programs of cultural events, high-tech laser light shows, and myriad of unique and colorful fireworks make this one of the area’s most popular festivals, drawing crowds of over 1 million visitors each year. Although most people flock to the beach for a closer view of the festivities, nearby Hwangnyeongsan Mountain, Dongbaekseom Island, and Igidae Coastal Park also offer great views of the fireworks.

title: Gwanak Starlight Walk

The event area spans 300-meters from Sillimgyo Bridge to Bongnimgyo Bridge. The diverse lighting artworks created by ten different Korean artist teams come together to create a space where stories of individuals all become one as a community. Various hands-on programs offer visitors a chance to see and enjoy the sights and sounds of the city throughout the festival period.

title: Gwanghwamun Market

title: Suseong Light Art Festival
overview: The Suseong Light Art Festival unfolds a feast of light every year with different themes, adorning Suseongmot Lake with colorful illuminations. It also features a variety of events, including an artwork exhibition and a drone art show.

title: Oh Slow Vintage Market
titleFull: Oh Slow Vintage Market (오슬로우 빈티지 마켓)
overview: Oh Slow Vintage Market is the largest vintage market in Korea for those who pursue a slow life, with numerous teams participating in the market, including vintage, antique, second-hand, flower, and small items that align with the values of "slow life." The market is characterized by vintage items and furniture that have been around for a long time and have their own unique value, as well as rare antique items that have their own history and timeless beauty. Quality second-hand clothing and miscellaneous goods provide opportunities to purchase brand products or items in good condition at reasonable prices, going beyond just low prices. The flower section includes fresh flowers and pots for adding a personal touch. Additionally, there are stylish design items and beautifully crafted handmade crafts that enrich lifestyles. Visitors can enjoy an exciting atmosphere with DJ performances and can learn about participating vintage businesses and rare vintage products in detail through a vintage docent tour.

title: Yeosu Hyangiram Sunrise Festival
addr: 60 Hyangiram-ro, Dolsan-eup, Yeosu-si, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Hyangiram Sunrise Festival is an annual overnight festival that begins on New Year's Eve. It takes place at the historic Hyangiram Hermitage, which was built in the year 644. As the New Year's Day dawns, visitors can witness the sun rise above the horizon from Hyangiram, which literally means "a hermitage facing the sun."

title: Homigot Sunrise Festival
overview:
Homigot Village, the main venue of the Homigot Sunrise Festival, is located on the easternmost point of the Korean Peninsula. Homigot Village means "a village on a tiger’s tail," in reference to the Korean peninsula looking like a tiger.

The festival includes local cultural performances, a New Year celebratory event, fireworks show, sunrise concert and other diverse performances. Visitors may sample free tteokguk, a traditional New Year’s Day dish. Other events such as kite-flying and launching hope balloons with wishes attached will provide enjoyable moments to reflect on the previous year and create new year resolutions.

title: Jeongdongjin Sunrise Festival
overview:
Many people come to celebrate a fresh start at the Jeongdongjin Sunrise Festival on the eve of one year and the first day of the New Year at Sandglass Park. The sandglass at the park has a diameter of 8.06 meters, a x_width of 3.2 meters, a weight of 40 tons, and holds 8 tons of sand, making it one of the biggest sandglasses in the world. It takes a whole year for sand to trickle to the bottom and then the sandglass restarts again on New Year’s Day each year at midnight.

Festival events include a fireworks display, the turning of the sandglass to start another year, and performances by various artists.

title: Namsan Beacon Ceremony and Traditional Culture Events
overview: In the Joseon era, the beacon mound on Namsan was the final relay point of a nationwide signal-fire network that carried news to the capital. This Seoul city program brings that system back to life: watch the beacon-lighting ceremony with historical commentary at the Namsan beacon site, join the daily noon bell-ringing at Bosingak Pavilion, and catch samulnori percussion and traditional martial-arts demonstrations at the Palgakjeong plaza by N Seoul Tower. Day programs let visitors try the night-watch and beacon-keeper roles themselves.
place: Namsan Beacon Mound and Bosingak Pavilion

title: Gugak Performance Jinyeon
overview: The gugak performance “Jinyeon, The Music of the Royal Banquet” offers a unique opportunity to experience the diversity of traditional Korean arts on a single stage. Set in an intimate venue designed in the style of a traditional Korean house, it allows for close interaction between the audience and performers. The program features a wide range of music performed on traditional instruments, spanning Korean music, K-pop, classical pieces, and world folk songs. As an all-in-one performance, it brings together elements of Korean culture, sound, instruments, and live performance into a single immersive experience.
fee: General admission 65,000 won Free admission: Children younger than 24 months old

title: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
titleFull: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show (광안리 M(Marvelous) 드론 라이트쇼)
overview: Every Saturday evening, 1,100 drones light up the night sky over Gwangallihaebyeon Beach in a range of fascinating formations through the Gwangalli M (Marvelous) Drone Light Show. The show takes place twice, with  each show taking around 12 minutes. On special occasions such as during Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving Day) or New Year's countdown, an even more spectacular show takes place featuring up to 3,000 drones.  * Schedule subject to change depending on weather conditions.

title: Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony at Deoksugung Palace
overview: The Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony is Seoul's flagship historical reenactment: the changing of the sumungun, the guards who kept the gates of Joseon-era palaces. Reconstructed from historical records, the ceremony unfolds in front of Daehanmun Gate at Deoksugung Palace, six days a week (closed Mondays) at 11:00 and 14:00. Hands-on programs run alongside it — beat the drum that opens the ceremony, dress as a gate guard yourself, or put on Joseon-era costume for photos. It is free, central, and one of the easiest ways to see living Joseon court ritual in the middle of modern Seoul.
place: In front of Daehanmun Gate, Deoksugung Palace

title: DDP Architecture Tour
overview: A guided walk through Dongdaemun Design Plaza, the landmark designed by Zaha Hadid, covering both the building itself and the history of the Dongdaemun area it sits in. Tours run Tuesday through Sunday (closed Mondays and on New Year's Day, Seollal, and Chuseok). The English tour departs at 13:30; Korean tours run at 10:30 and 15:30. Meet at the tour desk on the first floor of the DDP Museum; the walk takes about 60 minutes. Ages 13 and up; children under 13 must be accompanied by a guardian. Book online via the DDP website, or take a remaining spot on site from 10 minutes before departure.
fee: Adults 10,000 won · Veterans, military, visitors with disabilities, youth groups 8,000 won · Children 5,000 won

title: Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony 2026
overview: Pasu — standing guard over the capital's walls — was one of the key military rituals of the Joseon dynasty, and this reenactment restores it at Sungnyemun, Korea's National Treasure gate. Guards line up before the gate, the timekeeper announces the hour, conch and trumpet signals sound, and the gate-opening ritual begins on the commander's order, followed by six rounds of guard duty and shift changes before the closing ritual. Runs daily except Mondays, 10:00–15:40, free of charge — an easy add-on to any walk between Seoul Station and Myeong-dong.

title: Walk of the Royal Family
overview: A palace procession inside an airport: before your flight out of Incheon International, you can watch a reenactment of Joseon court life. In Terminal 1, the king and queen stroll the concourse as if walking the palace grounds; in Terminal 2, a royal procession with military officials recreates a late-Joseon martial exam visit. After each performance, visitors can take photos with the cast in full court dress. A rare chance to see Joseon pageantry without leaving the departures hall.

title: Pyeongchang Trout Festival
overview: In the past, winters in this region were unforgiving. Heavy snowfalls buried villages, and neighbors would stretch ropes between their homes, carving tunnels through the snow to find their way from one house to another. When the bitter winds sweeping across the river caused the shallow channels to freeze and merge early in the season, people would hammer at large rocks beneath the ice catch fish and secure a precious meal. Today, the hardships endured by our ancestors have been transformed into celebration. Every year from late December through late January, the Pyeongchang Trout Festival brings this winter heritage to life under the theme, “A Winter Story of Snow, Ice, and Trout.” Visitors can experience the thrill of trout fishing on the frozen Odaecheon Stream, where the crystal-clear ice reveals fish swimming beneath the surface. Along with a variety of winter activities, the festival offers an opportunity to enjoy the true charm and excitement of a Korean winter.

title: Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival
titleFull: Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival (철원 한탄강 얼음트레킹 축제)
overview: Set amid the spectacular winter landscape of the Hantangang River, the Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival is one of Cheorwon’s premier winter celebrations. The festival has been inducted into the Hall of Fame of the Korea Festival Contents Awards and was selected as an Outstanding Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for 2026–2027. Connected to the Hantangang River Mulwit-gil trekking course, the festival allows visitors to enjoy the river’s breathtaking snowy scenery while taking part in a variety of performances and winter-themed activities held throughout the festival period at the main venue beneath Seungilgyo Bridge. Special events, including the popular “Ttongbaram Altong Road Run," add to the festive atmosphere and excitement.

title: Daegwallyeong Snow Festival
overview: The Daegwallyeong Snow Festival is held in Daegwallyeong, Pyeongchang every January. Daegwallyeong Snow Festival first began in 1993 and was one of the first snow festivals that took place at the time. Since then it has become a prominent winter festival of the region that brings the community together. The festival's beautiful snowy hills and enjoyable activities are the perfect combination for bringing out the child in everyone.

title: 2026 Visit Korean Islands Year

It ties into the 2026 Yeosu World Island Exhibition — the first world expo dedicated to islands — and spreads the momentum nationwide with island travel subsidies, culture weeks, and events running throughout the year. If island-hopping in the South Sea archipelago is on your list, 2026 is the year the infrastructure, discounts, and programming all line up.

overview:
Ssokssokdeul-i Festival is a program organized by the National Theater of Korea’s Stage Arts Support Center, designed to make performing arts more accessible in everyday life. Held regularly throughout the year, it offers a variety of performances free of charge, creating greater opportunities for the public to engage with the arts in a relaxed and approachable setting.

The festival takes place at the “Ssok” Experience Theater within the Stage Arts Support Center and features dynamic stages that can be enjoyed by audiences of all ages. Tickets for the performances are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis at the on-site information desk starting at 12:00 on the day of the performance. These tickets may close early depending on the number of seats available. With artists presenting distinctive styles across a range of popular genres, it creates a vibrant cultural space where different generations can come together and share the experience.

title: Nonsan Strawberry Festival
overview: Held every year in Nonsan, Chungcheongnam-do, the Nonsan Strawberry Festival is one of Korea’s premier festivals celebrating a regional specialty. As the nation’s leading strawberry-producing area, Nonsan has built a stable production base and efficient distribution network. Building on these strengths, the festival has evolved into an industry-oriented event that integrates agriculture, food processing, and tourism. The festival features strawberry sales and tastings, hands-on experience programs, performances, exhibitions, and industry networking events. It is distinguished by the active participation of local farmers and small business owners, who play a central role in its operation. Designated as a Cultural Tourism Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for 2026–2027, the festival is also expanding its international reach and strengthening industry partnerships in preparation for the 2027 International Strawberry Industry Expo.

title: Goryeong Daegaya Festival
overview: The Goryeong Daegaya Festival is the Goryeong's flagship festival and a long-standing celebration where visitors can explore and experience the unique history and culture of Daegaya. In 2025, Goryeong was officially designated as the ancient capital of Daegaya, further enhancing the significance of its rich historical and cultural heritage. In addition, the discovery of pottery bearing the inscription “Great King” at the moat of the Daegaya Palace Site provided important evidence that Daegaya was a powerful ancient kingdom. Together with the inscription of the Jisandong Ancient Tombs on the UNESCO World Heritage List, these developments underscore the importance of preserving and promoting Daegaya’s history and culture for future generations. Under the theme “Daegaya Begins Again: RE-BORN,” the 2026 Goryeong Daegaya Festival seeks to foster pride in Goryeong’s status as the ancient capital of Daegaya while continuing to grow as a leading festival celebrating history and cultural heritage.

title: Jinhae Gunhangje Festival
overview: The Jinhae Gunhangje Festival is one of Korea's most iconic spring festivals. It began in 1952 as a memorial ceremony honoring Admiral Yi Sun-sin and developed into a full-fledged festival in 1963. Today, the festival attracts more than two million visitors from Korea and around the world each year. During the festival season, approximately 360,000 King cherry trees burst into bloom across Jinhae, creating one of Korea's most spectacular spring landscapes. Centered around Jungwon Rotary and Bugwon Rotary, the festival features a variety of events including the eve celebration, memorial rite, and the Victory Parade. A particular highlight is the Military Band and Honor Guard Festival, a signature Gunhangje event held on Friday evenings and throughout the weekends during the festival period. Visitors also have the rare opportunity to enter the Korea Naval Academy and the Naval Base Command in Jinhae, both of which are normally closed to the public. In addition, they can visit famous cherry blossom destinations such as Yeojwacheon Stream and Gyeonghwa Station, while exploring the century-old modern cultural heritage sites surrounding Jungwon Rotary. Together, these attractions offer a unique journey through the history, culture, and tranquil scenery of Korea’s historic naval city. Combining the beauty of cherry blossoms, the traditions of the Korean Navy, and the charm of modern history, Jinhae Gunhangje Festival offers an unforgettable celebration of spring.

title: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road
titleFull: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road (인천개항장 페스타 - 1901 라이브로드)
overview: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road is an urban music festival planned based on the historical significance and identity of Incheon Jemulpo, the original name of Incheon Open Port, and the birthplace of Western music exchange during the port's opening period. The show takes place throughout the cultural district of the open port, including the Sangsang Platform and Jemulpo Club. The performances feature a variety of genres, including jazz, folk, band, and EDM. By combining live performances, public participation, and the distinctive atmosphere of the historic port district, the festival offers a unique cultural experience that highlights Incheon’s urban heritage.

title: 2026 Culture Day: Cheongchun Mic (Seoul, Gyeonggi & Gangwon)
overview: The capital-region and Gangwon leg of Cheongchun Mic, Korea's Culture Day street-performance program. Young and senior performing teams selected by open call take their acts to streets and plazas across Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon from April through November. Expect anything from acoustic sets to dance crews — free, outdoors, and deliberately placed where people already are.

title: Nodeul Spring Preview Festival
titleFull: Nodeul Spring Preview Festival (노들 미리봄 페스티벌)

Various programs are prepared, including invited lectures, media exhibitions, talk shows, and artist performances. In addition, the festival explores how Nodeul Island can expand its purpose and cultural experiences under its new role as "Nodeul Global Art Island."

title: Icheon Baeksa Sansuyu Flower Festival
titleFull: Icheon Baeksa Sansuyu Flower Festival (이천백사 산수유꽃축제)
overview: Icheon’s Baeksa Village is home to a number of sansuyu (cornus fruit) trees, which have been growing naturally in the area for over 100 years. In early spring, the trees change colors to a striking bright yellow, whilst in autumn the village is filled with the trees’ vivid red fruits. During the festival, visitors can participate in Korean traditional folk games and watch the Sansuyu flower parade. When sansuyu trees blossom, many professional photographers travel to Baeksa Village to take pictures of this beautiful sight.

title: 2026 International Seon Meditation Conference
overview: Hosted by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, this conference-and-festival pairing explores Seon (Zen) meditation as a tool for mental health, now in its third year. The 2026 theme is 'Seon Meditation in the Age of AI'. Alongside the conference sessions, a public meditation festival at Bongeunsa Temple lets visitors try various forms of Seon practice first-hand — in one of the few major temples standing directly across from Gangnam's COEX skyline.
place: Bongeunsa Temple and Bongeun Culture Center

title: Yeongam Wangin Culture Festival
addr: 440, Wangin-ro, Gunseo-myeon, Yeongam-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: First held in 1997, the Yeongam Wangin Culture Festival is one of Korea’s leading Cultural Tourism Festivals and has been held every spring at the Historical Site of Wangin. Dr. Wangin played a pivotal role in cultural exchange across ancient East Asia. Through him, Baekje’s advanced culture and Confucian classics crossed the Korea Strait and reached the Japanese archipelago. His teachings represented far more than a transfer of knowledge; they became a driving force behind the emergence of Asuka culture, the golden age of ancient Japanese civilization. Wangin’s profound scholarship, together with the flowing Yeongsangang River and Sangdaepo Port, symbolizes the currents of exchange that carried culture across the sea. Here in Yeongam, visitors can rediscover the roots of Asuka culture.

title: Chungjang Raon Festa 2026
overview: A monthly street festival in Gwangju's Chungjang-ro shopping district, running the first Saturday of each month from April. Launched in 2022 to revive the downtown commercial area, it layers culture and hands-on programs over the streets and underground arcade — music, markets, and family-friendly events. Times vary by program; the district itself is Gwangju's classic downtown, dense with shops and street food.

The name Geotjaing blends the local dialect for 'let's walk' with '-ing'. The street fills with walkers, pop-up culture programs, and performances, part of the city's push toward transit, cycling, and walking. A good date to aim for if you want to see downtown Gwangju at its liveliest.

title: Daejeon Science Festival
overview: Held in conjunction with the 2026 Korea Science Festival, the Daejeon Science Festival is Korea’s largest science event, co-hosted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and Daejeon Metropolitan City. The festival invites visitors to experience how advances in science and technology are transforming everyday life while encouraging them to explore and prepare for the future together. Government agencies, public institutions, private companies, and organizations participate in the event, presenting a wide range of programs, including exhibitions, hands-on experiences, performances, lectures, and competitions. Covering everything from cutting-edge technologies to the science embedded in everyday life, the festival offers engaging programs and content for visitors of all ages, from students to adults. More than Korea’s premier science festival, it continues to evolve as a people-centered urban festival and a leading global platform for science and technology culture.

title: Culture Lounge Gyeonggi-Jang
overview: A hands-on cultural space in Suwon showcasing local content from across Gyeonggi Province in one place. 'Local Radar' builds a personalized Gyeonggi travel plan around your tastes; the 'Gyeonggi Ceramics Shop' combines pottery-craft experiences with tea tasting. The space mixes exhibition, performance, and participation — less a museum than a browsing room for what the province around Seoul has to offer.

overview: The Jeonju Hanok Village Traditional Performance Parade is packed with various street performances, allowing visitors to experience Jeonju's folk culture on the streets. During the parade, visitors can witness Jeonju gijeopnori, a representative traditional performance of Jeonju; madangnori, a traditional performance featuring dance, music, and storytelling through various forms, or sing along to folk labor songs.

title: Hangang River History Tour
overview: Guided walking tours along the Han River, pairing riverside scenery with the history layered around it. Sixteen courses cover different stretches of the river and nearby heritage sites, each led by a Hangang interpreter. Tours run in two daily slots (10:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00) and take about two hours. It is one of the simplest ways to turn a riverside walk into something with a storyline — though note the commentary is primarily in Korean.

title: Hampyeong Butterfly Festival
addr: 27, Gonjae-ro, Hampyeong-eup, Hampyeong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The 28th Hampyeong Butterfly Festival will be held under the theme “Dreaming Butterflies, A Journey Begins.” This year’s festival captures the atmosphere of a special spring picnic, featuring vibrant displays of flowers and butterflies throughout the venue. Surrounded by colorful blooms and fluttering butterflies, visitors can enjoy a variety of hands-on activities and performances that celebrate the beauty of life and nature. It is the perfect spring outing for families, couples, and friends to share joyful moments and create lasting memories together.

title: Icheon Ceramics Festival
overview: The 40th Icheon Ceramic Festival is a celebration of ceramic culture held at Icheon Ceramics Village and throughout Sagimakgol Pottery Village in Icheon, Gyeonggi-do. Renowned for its high-quality clay and advanced kiln techniques, Icheon has long been one of Korea’s leading ceramic centers, preserving and advancing a ceramic tradition that bridges the past and the present. Marking its 40th anniversary, this year’s festival reflects on the history and significance of the Icheon Ceramic Festival while exploring new directions for the future of ceramic culture. During the festival, ceramic artists and visitors come together to share the artistic value of ceramics and experience the creative process firsthand through programs such as pottery wheel workshops and wish-writing activities on large ceramic pieces. The festival also features a wide range of exhibitions and sales, showcasing everything from traditional pottery to contemporary ceramic art. Academic seminars, competitions, and performances further expand the festival's role as a platform for cultural and artistic exchange. Through the active participation of local ceramic artists and residents, the festival contributes to the local economy while sharing the excellence of Icheon’s ceramic culture with the world.

In addition, the expo features vibrant outdoor attractions, including themed gardens, a healing garden, and a symbolic clock tower. Held in spring, the expo offers a wonderful opportunity for families to enjoy nature while discovering the healing power of horticulture.

title: Goesan Space City: Star Explorers
overview: A hands-on children's exhibition at the Goesan Eco Museum built around an imagined 'space ecology', exploring fruits and plants through seeing, touching, and moving. Kids question, imagine, and build their own stories through the interactive course, with parents cast as fellow guides on the expedition. A useful rainy-day or family stop if you are in the Chungbuk countryside.

title: Ulsan Onggi Festival
overview: The Ulsan Onggi Festival is Korea’s only festival dedicated to onggi, the traditional earthenware that has been an integral part of Korean life for more than a thousand years. Held in Oegosan Onggi Village in Ulju-gun, where artisans continue to produce onggi using traditional techniques, the festival naturally serves as a showcase the region’s signature craft. It also contributes to the promotion of everyday onggi use and the continued development of this traditional industry. Visitors can enjoy onggi-making demonstrations by master artisans, as well as a variety of hands-on programs, exhibitions, and performances.

title: Seoul Street Performance: Every Corner Live 2026
overview: 150 artist teams selected by open call perform across central Seoul's streets and plazas through late November. The point is the surprise: performances appear where people already are — station exits, plazas, park corners — rather than on ticketed stages. Free by nature; times and spots vary by performance.

title: Boseong Green Tea Festival
addr: 775, Nokcha-ro, Boseong-eup, Boseong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Celebrating its 49th year, the Boseong Green Tea Festival will be held this year under the theme of Boseong Matcha. In today's fast-paced world, where the need for rest and rejuvenation is greater than ever, visitors can recharge both body and mind amid the tranquility of the region's lush green tea fields. Set against the breathtaking backdrop of emerald tea plantations, the festival offers a variety of tea-themed experiences, including tea leaf picking, tea making, creating and enjoying personalized tea blends, and green tea therapy programs. Through these immersive activities, visitors can fully experience the physical, emotional, and mental benefits of green tea.
place: Korean Tea Culture Park & Boseong tea fields

title: Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival
overview: The Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival is held every May in Hadong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, Korea’s first tea cultivation site. Designated by the government as an Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival, the festival celebrates Hadong’s wild tea, long renowned for its rich flavor and aroma and grown in the area’s pristine natural environment. Since hosting the Hadong World Tea Expo in 2023, Hadong has strengthened its identity as a “tea wellness culture city” and continued to enhance the value of its tea industry and culture. In 2026, the festival marks its 29th edition. Visit Hadong in May, when the landscape is at its freshest and greenest, and enjoy music and art programs such as “Busking in a Teacup” and “Melody on Tea Leaves,” along with healing programs including tea classes, book talks, and walks along the Horibyeong Byeolcheonji Trail. Here, a single cup of tea can turn an ordinary day into something special while allowing visitors experience the full flavor and charm of Hadong. This year, the festival will also feature a variety of Children’s Day programs for the whole family on May 5.
place: Hadong Wild Tea Healing Center (Tea Café Hadong), Hadong Wild Tea Museum
sponsor: Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival Organizing Committee

title: Damyang Bamboo Festival
addr: 130, Jungnogwon-ro, Damyang-eup, Damyang-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Held under the slogan “Shine Bright, Bamboo!” this year’s festival celebrates the spirit of bamboo with a message of hope. During the day, visitors can enjoy lively hands-on programs and performances. At night, the bamboo forest lights up, offering a completely different festival experience. The festival features a wide range of programs that bring together tradition and modern creativity. As visitors walk through the bamboo grove and listen to the wind moving through the trees, they can take in the history, culture, and natural beauty of Damyang. With family, couples, and friends, visitors can enjoy the beauty and calm of bamboo while reflecting on the value of sustainable nature. In the green bamboo forest, the festival offers bright, memorable moments filled with hope.
place: Damyang Sports Complex, Juknokwon, Dambit Music Hall

title: Hwaseong Haenggung Palace Night Opening 2026
overview: Hwaseong Haenggung — the grandest of Korea's temporary royal palaces, built for King Jeongjo's visits to Suwon — opens after dark for its signature night program, 'Moonlight Hwadam: Stories of Flowers under the Moon'. Flower installations and atmospheric lighting turn the palace courtyards into a slow evening walk, quieter and more intimate than daytime visits. It sits inside the UNESCO-listed Hwaseong Fortress, so you can pair it with a night walk on the fortress wall.
fee: Adults 2,000 won · Youth/military 1,500 won · Children 1,000 won

title: Mungyeong Chasabal Festival
overview: Celebrating its 28th edition, the 2026 Mungyeong Chasabal (Tea Bowl) Festival is one of Korea’s leading festivals, where deep-rooted tradition meets contemporary creativity. The festival will run for ten days from May 1 to 10, 2026, at the Mungyeongsaejae Open Set, surrounded by the area’s stunning natural scenery. Mungyeong ceramics are crafted in traditional wood-fired mangdaengi kilns and fired at temperatures exceeding 1,300°C. Rather than relying on elaborate decoration, they are known for their rustic, natural beauty. Chasabal tea bowls possess a quiet charm that brings a sense of calm to those who use them. This year’s festival will offer even more hands-on programs for Millennial and Gen Z visitors and families. With more opportunities to participate, stay, and explore, the festival continues to evolve into an immersive experience visitors can truly be part of.

title: Hangang Night View Tour
overview: A relaxed guided night walk along the Han River with stories behind the skyline, on two courses: the Banpo Moonlight Course (Seorae Island, Some Sevit, the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, and Jamsugyo Bridge) and the Yeouido Starlight Course (Hangang Art Park, Mapo Bridge, the floating stage, and the water-light plaza). Runs Friday and Saturday evenings, 19:00–20:30. Free, but spots are allocated by lottery.

title: Yeoncheon Paleolithic Festival
overview: The Yeoncheon Paleolithic Festival is a hands-on prehistoric culture festival held at the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site in Yeoncheon, where some of the earliest humans on the Korean Peninsula once lived. The site is world-renowned for the discovery of Acheulean hand axes, evidence that highly advanced Paleolithic people inhabited Korea some 300,000 years ago. Once a year, Jeongok-ri becomes a gathering place for prehistoric cultures from around the world, inviting modern visitors to step into the world of early human life through a wide range of immersive experiences. Rooted in the historical significance of the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site, the festival promotes harmony between cultural heritage and the public, strengthens the region’s identity, and demonstrates how archaeological sites can be actively preserved while being brought to life.

title: Hangang River Festival
overview: In May, the Hangang River offers a range of activities that appeal to both children and adults. Programs include plays based on Korea's folklore, as well as family-friendly experiences. Visitors can also participate in silent yoga sessions using headsets or enjoy the natural scenery of Seoul through activities such as kayaking, yachting, and river cruises. These programs provide a variety of ways to experience the Hangang River during the spring season.
place: Ichon Hangang Park next to Parking Lot 3 grassy area
fee: Free (Separate fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Culture Flows at Seoul Plaza
overview: Free open-air concerts on the outdoor stage at Seoul Plaza, running roughly eight months from May to December. The 2026 season opens on May 6 and cycles through pop, hip-hop, jazz, bands, and performance acts month by month, in the plaza in front of City Hall — easy to fold into any evening downtown.

title: Chunhyang Festival
overview: Taking place in Namwon, Chunhyang Festival celebrates the love between Chunhyang and Lee Mongryong, based on the famous Korean love story, Chunhyangjeon. Held since 1931, the festival aims to spread the story not only around Korea but to international visitors as well through hands-on experiences and moving performances. The highlight of the festival is the beauty pageant that attracts many people.
fee: Free (fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Miryang Arirang Festival
overview: The Miryang Arirang Festival celebrates and preserves Miryang Arirang, which was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2012. First launched in 1957 as the Miryang Cultural Festival, it has grown into one of Gyeongsangnam-do’s leading regional festivals. Visitors can enjoy the Miryang Arirang Competition, Arirang-themed experiences, and a variety of traditional cultural programs. The highlight of the festival is Miryanggang Odyssey, a fantasy musical brings together thousands of years of Miryang’s history and the spirit of Miryang Arirang. Featuring spectacular performances, beautiful music, and captivating storytelling, the production leaves a lasting impression on audiences and stands as one of the festival's signature attractions.
place: Yeongnamnu Pavilion, Miryanggang Riverside, Namcheongangbyeon-ro, Naeil-dong Shopping District

title: Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival
titleFull: Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival (두위봉 철쭉축제&산맥페스티벌)
overview: During the Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival, visitors can walk along azalea-lined mountain trails and unwind by clear valley streams during the day, then enjoy live performances and DJ sets in the evening. They can also visit the Arirang exhibition at the historic former National Land Development Corps building for a closer look at Jeongseon Arirang and the area’s local history. A range of hands-on activities, including wellness programs and bracelet-making, is available, along with beer and local food zones offering regional specialties and craft brews.
place: Uirimgil Daebak Market and Dangokgyegok Valley in Sindong-eup

title: Mokpo Marine W Show 2026
overview: Mokpo's flagship night show and one of the signature attractions of this southern port city: a multimedia performance combining a floating sea stage, Korea's largest marine fountain, and fireworks over the water. Over five years it has drawn more than a million viewers across 51 shows. The 2026 edition scales up the sea-stage performances, fireworks, and choreographed fountain work. Free viewing from Peace Plaza on the waterfront.

title: Sunyang Barefoot Festa
overview: Sunyang Barefoot Festa is an exclusive festival that participants can walk or run barefoot along the red clay trail while enjoying a cultural experience. Feet are thought to be the second heart in our body as it connects the entire living being. Moreover, stimulating the feet by walking on clay road are known to have positive health benefits such as preventing and healing diseases, and stress relieving. This event invites people of all ages to participate in a healthy and fun walking festival where attendees can admire the beautiful nature scenery as well as take part in various entertaining programs.
place: Jangdong Forest Park in Gyejoksan Mountain

title: Haeundae Sand Festival
overview: Held every year between May and June, the Haeundae Sand Festival is Korea’s largest sand festival. Set on Haeundae Beach, one of the nation's most iconic seaside destinations, the festival celebrates the beauty of Haeundae and highlights the value of sand as an important marine resource. Each year, world-class sand sculptures, hands-on programs, and performances are presented under a new theme. In 2026, the festival will be held under the theme “Busan,” showcasing the city’s dynamic transformation from past to present and into the future, while highlighting the unique charm that has captivated visitors from around the world. The festival runs from May 15 to 18, while the sand sculpture exhibition will remain open through June 14.

title: Yeon Deung Hoe
overview: Started approximately 1,200 years ago during the Silla dynasty and continued through the Goryeo Yeon Deung Hoe and Joseon lantern festival, the Yeon Deung Hoe Festival is a traditional festival registered as an Intangible Cultural Heritage and UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity. The lanterns at Yeon Deung Hoe Festival brighten the heart and the world!

title: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival
titleFull: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival (하늘숲길 걷기축제)
overview: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival (Haneulsupgil Walking Festival) is a family-friendly forest festival held along the Sky Forest Trail at an altitude of 1,300 meters. Visitors can explore the area’s rich natural environment, including native trees, wildflowers, insects, and various plant species, making it an especially enjoyable experience for children and families. The festival features well-maintained walking trails converted from former coal transport routes, offering safe trekking courses suitable for participants of all ages, along with forest-themed experiential programs. Surrounded by pristine nature, the festival provides a relaxing opportunity to unwind and enjoy healing time outdoors.
fee: Participation fee 15,000 won* Free for children under 24 months old

title: Gokseong International Rose Festival
addr: 232 Gichamaeul-ro, Ogok-myeon, Gokseong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Gokseong International Rose Festival is a vibrant spring celebration featuring 1,004 varieties of roses, including rare European species and famous roses from around the globe. Held at the landmark Gokseong Train Village, the festival is filled with the romantic fragrance of roses.

title: Busan Old Town Revitalization Festival [Taxchelin]
overview: Enjoy the charm of of Busan's old downtown through "Taxchelin!" Taxulain is a combination of taxi and Michelin, and it is a festival where you can enjoy performances, experiences, and tours centered around local hidden gems recommended by veteran taxi drivers with over 10 years of experience. The festival highlights on a  different theme each year, making every moment special.

title: Hwaseong Boating Festival
overview: The Hwaseong Boating Festival, Hwaseong’s signature festival, is the largest marine cultural event in the Seoul metropolitan area. Visitors can experience a variety of activities on the waters of the West Sea, including sailing yachts, powerboats, marine cable cars, and the Voyage of the Pungnyudan. The festival also features the Messengers of the Wind dance parade, showcasing the energy and enthusiasm of local residents, as well as spectacular performances and fireworks that light up the night sky. From mudflat ecology programs and traditional fish-trap experiences to a large beach playground and marine plogging, the festival offers a diverse range of attractions and activities both on land and at sea.

title: Jeju Food and Wine Festival
overview: The Jeju Food & Wine Festival (JFWF), Jeju’s premier gastronomic festival, is a cultural event that showcases the value of Jeju’s local ingredients and culinary heritage to both domestic and international audiences through dishes crafted from the island’s pristine produce. The festival presents a diverse program of culinary experiences, including Gala Dinners featuring multi-course fine dining by renowned chefs, and Gourmet Week, which highlights collaborations with chefs, celebrities, and brands at leading local establishments. Signature ingredients of Jeju, such as its famed pork, are showcased through curated dining events led by top restaurants and guest chefs. Visitors can also take part in interactive cooking classes, dessert and café showcases, and other programs that allow one to fully experience Jeju's gastronomic culture.
fee: * Refer to the official website for details
sponsor: Jeju Food & Wine Festival Organizing Committee

title: Chuncheon Mime Festival
overview: The Chuncheon Mime Festival is one of Korea’s leading performing arts festivals, connecting the city, art, and its people through mime, an art form that communicates through movement. Held every year during the last week of May in Chuncheon, the city of water and springtime, the festival is recognized as one of the world’s three major mime festivals, alongside France’s Mimos Mime Festival and the London Mime Festival in the United Kingdom. Over the years, it has developed a distinctive artistic identity that blends Chuncheon, mime, and festival culture into a genre of its own. Through wordless movement and the creative fusion of water, fire, flowers, light, video, and other artistic forms, the festival expresses the emotions and spirit of the city and its people. It is also a vibrant “nanjang” festival that transforms the desires and energies of both the city and the times into artistic expression. Under the theme “Body Landscape,” the 2026 Chuncheon Mime Festival will take place from May 24 to 31. Beginning with the opening nanjang, Ah! Surajang, the eight-day festival will present diverse "body landscapes" throughout Chuncheon through theater performances, Walking Mime, Art Nanjang X, and the all-night Dokkaebi Nanjang.
place: Festival Theater MIME and other locations across Chuncheon
sponsor: Chuncheon Mime Festival, KBS Chuncheon Broadcasting Center

title: Imsil N Rose Festival
overview:
The Imsil N Rose Festival is a spring event held in the Rose Garden at Imsil Cheese Theme Park in Imsil-gun, Jeonbuk State. Set within a 65,705 ㎡ rose garden showcasing over 150 varieties and more than 22,000 rose plants, the festival is designed as a tourism-focused event that integrates performances, hands-on experiences, and food offerings.

Featuring a rose-themed parade and performances, interactive programs, and local agricultural and specialty products, it seeks to provide visitors with a rich and engaging experience while supporting the local economy and strengthening the region’s tourism brand. As an inaugural festival, it also captures a unique sense of freshness and anticipation, offering an emotionally engaging springtime experience that encourages longer stays through immersive, rose-inspired content and participatory activities.

title: Pyeonghwa Ondam
overview:
“Peace On: Dam” in Dongtan is a cultural event designed to bring the theme of “peace,” which often feels distant, into everyday life. As part of the regional peace consensus-building project first launched by the Ministry of Unification in 2026, the event provides an opportunity to engage with the concepts of peace and unification in a familiar, local setting.

Held near residential communities, the event invites residents to participate in a variety of cultural experiences, share stories with family and neighbors, and reflect on topics that are not often considered in daily routines.

At the venue, visitors of all ages can enjoy a diverse lineup of hands-on programs, performances, and interactive activities. Through moments of laughter, creativity, and connection, “Peace On: Dam” fosters a warm and welcoming festival atmosphere that encourages a renewed appreciation for peace through small but meaningful experiences.

title: Cheongju Pet Culture Event
titleFull: Cheongju Pet Culture Event (청주시 반려동물 문화행사 )
overview: The Cheongju Pet Culture Event “School Bell Ring Ring Ring” takes place on the spacious lawn of Chungbuk Health and Science University. The open setting provides a safe and comfortable environment where children can run freely, while professional programs organized by the Department of Pet Culture offer structured and engaging activities.  The event creates opportunities for pet owners to connect with one another and participate in a variety of hands-on experience programs, all within the pleasant surroundings of the university campus. Designed with families in mind, it offers an inclusive atmosphere that welcomes visitors of all ages.
place: Chungbuk Health and Science University Lawn
fee: Free (some booths may require a participation fee)
sponsor: Chungbuk Health Science University Department of Pet Culture

title: Palsaek Chanran: Regions Full of K
overview: A special exhibition at the Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae asking where the 'K' in K-culture actually comes from. Through regional-content displays and media art, it traces how local histories, arts, and cultural assets across Korea's provinces feed into today's K-content — an argument that hallyu's roots run through the regions, not just Seoul. Runs through December on the first floor of Sarangchae, next to the former presidential compound.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Port Village Busan
overview: Port Village Busan takes place at Pier 1 of Busan Port, transforming a 4,300-pyeong site (approximately 14,200 ㎡) into a unique underwater-themed village. The event will bring together over 60 of Busan’s most popular local brands. Visitors can explore everything from limited-edition foods available only within this mysterious “underwater village” to signature menus from well-loved eateries. The market will also feature a curated living and lifestyle shop, along with a variety of pop-up stores. As a large-scale, 12-day market, Port Village Busan offers an exclusive opportunity to experience a diverse range of food, shopping, and activities centered around its immersive underwater theme.
sponsor: Food Travel Co., Busan Tourism Organization

title: Jeju International Tourism Marathon Festival
overview: The Jeju International Tourism Marathon Festival, which began in 1995, is the first citizen-participation marathon in Korea that allows the general public to participate. It is a sports festival that can be enjoyed by people of all ages, families, and couples, featuring a marathon course along the beautiful coastline of Jeju.
fee: FULL (42.195 km) 50,000 wonHALF (21.0975 km) 50,000 wonGeneral course (10 km) 40,000 won

title: Eumseong Pumba Festival
overview: The Eumseong Pumba Festival is rooted in the life of the late Choi Gwi-dong, often remembered as a saint of compassion and love. Although he lived with a disability himself, Choi traveled throughout Mugeuk-ri in Geumwang-eup collecting food—not for himself, but for beggars who were too weak even to beg. His life later inspired Father Oh Woong-jin to establish Kkottongnae, and his example of selfless service continues to inspire many today. Various explanations have been passed down regarding the origin of the word pumba. Traditionally, it refers to an onomatopoeic refrain used in gakseori taryeong, the songs associated with wandering performers and itinerant peddlers. The Eumseong Pumba Festival combines this traditional image of pumba with Choi Gwi-dong’s spirit of philanthropy and compassion. Although modern society enjoys greater material prosperity, spiritual emptiness and social inequality still remain. The festival was created around the idea that society can find catharsis through satire and humor and be healed through love and sharing. For this reason, the Eumseong Pumba Festival has become a unique cultural festival dedicated to putting the values of love, compassion, and sharing into practice.
place: Seolseong Park and Kkottongnae in Eumseong-eup

title: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef Festival
titleFull: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef Festival (남해 마늘한우축제)
overview: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef celebrates Namhae’s signature agricultural products: garlic and premium Korean beef. The festival takes place at the Namhae Exile Literature Museum, with five nearby parking areas for easy access. Visitors can browse and purchase a wide range of local specialties in one place, prepared by local farmers and fishermen, and enjoy the event alongside residents. There is a shuttle bus that takes passengers back and forth between the parking lot and the festival venue.

title: Hansan Ramie Fabric Cultural Festival
overview: The Hansan Ramie Fabric Cultural Festival is Korea’s leading eco-friendly traditional textile festival, celebrating Hansan Mosi Weaving, which is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Held every June around the Hansan Mosi Museum in Hansan-myeon, Seocheon-gun, the festival offers a variety of ramie-related cultural programs, including Hansan Mosi School, mini loom-weaving experiences, and Jeosanpal-eup Gilssamnori. Bringing together tradition, nature, and hands-on experiences, the festival offers visitors a unique opportunity to explore the history and artistry of Korea’s renowned ramie culture.

title: Gwangalli Eobang Festival
overview: The Suyeong area has long been rich in fishery resources and was one of the first places in Busan where fishing developed on a large scale. During the Joseon Dynasty, Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong Naval Command was established here, along with eobang, a cooperative fishing organization formed by local fishers and naval forces. The fishing practices of that era have been preserved and passed down through Jwasuyeong Eobang Nori, a traditional folk performance based on the work and customs of fishing communities. The Gwangalli Eobang Festival takes its name from this heritage. Celebrating the history of Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong and the folk traditions of Korea's coastal fishing villages, it has become one of Busan’s representative cultural festivals.
place: Gwangalli Beach and Suyeong Historical Park

title: N Seoul Tower Global Night Walk
titleFull: N Seoul Tower Global Night Walk (N서울타워 글로벌 나이트워크)
overview:
The N Seoul Tower Night Walk is a nighttime walking event that begins at Baekbeom Square and continues through the Seoul Education Research & Information Institute, Samsuni Stairs, Waryongmyo Shrine, Seokhojeong Pavilion, and the southern access road, before reaching N Seoul Tower Plaza. The program features an approximately 6-kilometer course, offering participants the opportunity to enjoy the night views of central Seoul and the surrounding landscapes of Namsan Mountain.

Before and after the walk, a variety of programs are available, including warm-up stretching sessions, live performances, interactive events, checkpoint rewards, completion rewards, on-site activities, and the Namsan Night Market. Participants also receive commemorative items such as a functional T-shirt, LED armband, handkerchief, storage bag, finisher’s medal, certificate, and a coupon pack.

title: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Riverside Concert
titleFull: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Riverside Concert (창립 65주년 기념 한국경제인협회와 함께하는 2026 서울시향 강변음악회)
overview:
To mark its 65th anniversary, the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra presents the “2026 Seoul Riverside Concert with the Federation of Korean Industries” on June 13 at Yeouido Hangang Park. The event brings together a full orchestral performance, appearances by world-class guest artists, and a fireworks finale.

Open to all free of charge, the concert offers a chance to experience live classical music alongside the nightscape of the Hangang River, creating a memorable and romantic evening in the heart of the city.

title: Taehwagang Maduhee Festival
overview: Maduhee is a traditional folk game rooted in Hakseongji, a historical record of Ulsan from the reign of King Yeongjo of the Joseon Dynasty. Through storytelling and historical interpretation, the festival reinforces the tradition and identity of Maduhee while evolving into a community-led tourism festival. By combining summer leisure activities along the Taehwagang River with lively evening programs such as the Chimaek (chicken and beer) Festival, it offers a unique seasonal experience. As the first major summer festival of the year in Korea, the Taehwagang Maduhee Festival provides a venue for community unity through the Maduhee Tug-of-War, in which citizens from across Ulsan take part. Held in the historic downtown area of Jung-gu, Ulsan, the 2026 festival features the grand Maduhee Tug-of-War, Water Tug-of-War on the Taehwagang River, the Chimaek Festival, EDM parties with DJs, ssireum (traditional Korean wrestling) competitions, and a variety of hands-on experiences.
place: Taehwagang Riverside and Seongnam-dong Area, Jung-gu, Ulsan

title: 2026 Culture Day: Culture Delivery
overview: A traveling arts program that brings street performances to places with the least access to culture — remote villages, border areas, and industrial districts across the capital region and Gangwon. Young and senior performing teams stage free shows in everyday local spaces from June to October, delivering the arts to audiences who rarely get them nearby.
place: Samgot-ri Village, Yeoncheon and other sites
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Busan Food Film Festa
overview: The Busan Food Film Festa is a unique cultural event that brings together film and food through a diverse range of programs and experiences. It offers an engaging platform where cinematic storytelling and culinary culture intersect. One of its signature programs, the Food Terrace, provides a setting to explore food-related themes in film while enjoying curated tastings guided by experts. The festival also features a flea market showcasing small businesses, a range of food trucks, and interactive programs such as pizza-making experiences suitable for families. With its rich blend of storytelling and gastronomy, the event offers a vibrant and memorable cultural experience.
fee: Free (separate fees may be required for certain programs)
hours: 12:00~20:00  *Please refer to the official website for detailed event times as they are subject to change.*
sponsor: Busan Food Film Festa Organizing Committee, Busan Cinema Center

title: Masterpieces and Teatime: A Cup of Calm in Light and Color
titleFull: 안다미로귀때박물관 기획전시 '명화와 티타임(Teatime) : 빛과 색채로 마시는 차 한 잔의 여유'
overview: A themed exhibition at the Andamiro Gwittae Museum pairing famous paintings of tea with the real teapots and cups depicted in them. When the Age of Exploration carried tea from Asia to Europe, it carried the vessels too — and painters began capturing the warmth of teatime in luminous color. From the quiet glow of William McGregor Paxton's 'Tea Leaves' to the silver teapot in Mary Cassatt's 'The Tea', the show lets you stand in front of the scene and the object at once.

title: Daegu Chimac Festival
overview: The Daegu Chimac Festival is Daegu’s signature summer festival and Korea’s largest food-and-drink event celebrating the much-loved pairing of chicken and beer. Since its launch in 2013, it has grown steadily, now drawing one million visitors and helping boost the local economy while raising Daegu’s profile as a global destination. Selected in 2026 for Korea’s Local 100 list and as a Preliminary Global Festival, this year’s event will run from July 1 to 5 in and around Duryu Park. Beyond chicken and beer, the festival offers a full lineup of performances, exhibitions, hands-on programs, and promotional booths. The main venue, 2.28 Freedom Square, will be transformed into a water concert zone where water play meets electronic music, with a new 360-degree central stage added this year. Across the festival grounds, visitors can explore themed zones such as Daefrica Waterpia, Chimac Sing-along Club, and Chisangnakwon EGG Island. Artist-designed installations and photo zones will bring even more energy to the festival grounds.
sponsor: Korean Chicken and Beer Industry Association

title: WSL Siheung Korea Open Qualifying Series
titleFull: WSL Siheung Korea Open Qualifying Series (WSL 시흥 코리아 오픈 국제 서핑대회)
overview:
The WSL Siheung Korea Open is held at Wave Park in Siheung, Asia’s largest artificial surfing facility, over three days. As Korea’s first official World Surf League (WSL) Qualifying Series event, and the first to take place in an artificial wave pool, it has drawn global attention from the surfing community. The venue features a 2,240-meter-long cove and can accommodate up to 160 athletes and 20,000 spectators.

The competition features top surfers from multiple countries across men’s and women’s shortboard and longboard divisions. Recognized as a key international event, it is broadcast in several countries and serves as an important stage for competitive surfing in the region. The event is hosted by the Siheung and organized in collaboration with local sports and media partners, with support from national and regional institutions.

title: Dancing Sangsoe: The Pilbong Gut Encounter
titleFull: Dancing Sangsoe: The Pilbong Gut Encounter(춤추는 상쇠〈만남〉)
place: Pilbong Cultural Village, 272, Gangun-ro, Imsil-gun, Jeonbuk-do

title: Busan Brand Festa
overview:
Busan Brand Festa is a large-scale consumer festival that highlights Busan, showcasing hidden gem brands from across the region and introducing them to both residents and visitors. This year’s event brings together over 190 leading local brands and well-known creators, offering a glimpse into the city’s diverse appeal.

In addition to local brand booths, the festival features a variety of programs, including a live drawing show by a popular webtoon artist and collaborative merchandise with well-known Busan-based food YouTubers. Visitors can also enjoy on-site cash coupon promotions and a range of events with prizes, creating a lively summer experience for friends and families alike.

title: Contemporary Artist Project: Lee Wan — I Write
overview: An exhibition at the Seoul Arts Center's Calligraphy Museum reinterpreting traditional Korean calligraphy through contemporary art. Working from brush and ink, artist Lee Wan combines script, image, painting, and seal-carving to push at what calligraphy can be — and asks not 'is the writing beautiful' but 'why do we write at all'. A compact, thoughtful show where tradition and contemporary practice meet.
place: Gallery 3, Calligraphy Museum, Seoul Arts Center

title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival

The 24th edition runs July 17 to October 11 across the DongGang Museum of Photography and venues around the county. Highlights include the DongGang Photography Award exhibition — this year featuring Im An-na — and an open-call international show of 19 photographers selected from worldwide submissions, alongside a full slate of themed exhibitions. Worth combining with Yeongwol's river valleys and the Jangneung royal tomb.

title: Miryang Performing Arts Festival

Selected by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the festival is designed to allow citizens and tourists to naturally encounter performances in their daily lives. Under the slogan "The City as a Stage, Daily Life as a Performance," the festival has significantly expanded its venues to include Miryang Arena, the Arirang Art Center, Eoreumgol Valley, and other locations throughout Miryang City. Diverse performances and rich events will take place during the festival period. From stages of warm empathy that bridge generations to unique immersive performances that boldly break down the barriers between stage and audience, a variety of theatrical performances blurring the boundaries between the audience and art are set to unfold against the backdrop of Miryang's beautiful nature and urban spaces.

title: Music in PyeongChang
overview: Music in PyeongChang is dedicated to inspire the audience with the passion for music and build a foundation for future musicians. The festival welcomes all who love music with a variety of music programs that take place among the beautiful nature of Gangwon State.

title: Texture of Rest
overview: The Wooran Foundation's second textile exhibition offers fiber art as an answer to modern overload. Taking textiles' inherent qualities — connection and patience — as its medium, the show frames weaving as a way of re-threading a scattered self: not avoiding difficulty but passing through it toward genuine rest. A quiet, meditative stop in Seongsu-dong, Seoul's converted-warehouse art district.

title: K-Illustration Fair Busan

title: K-Handmade Fair Busan
overview: The K-Handmade Fair serves as a platform for exchange between creators and consumers. It is also a space where visitors can explore the market trends and sustainability of creator brands. Held annually with a unique theme, the fair provides creators with an opportunity to showcase their products, while visitors can purchase trendy, high-quality handmade goods, check out DIY kits, and take part in various hands-on experience programs.

title: Boryeong Mud Festival
overview: The Boryeong Mud Festival is Korea’s leading global summer festival, where visitors can enjoy mud in every possible way. Overlooking the expansive Daecheon Beach, the festival features a variety of zones, from the General Zone for full-scale mud activities to the Family Zone and Water Park Zone, where visitors of all ages can cool off and have fun safely. During the day, mud attractions help beat the summer heat, including Mud Mob Scene, a one-of-a-kind program featuring DJ and EDM performances and blasts from mud water cannons. At night, the excitement continues with a spectacular drone show over the sea and large-scale evening performances. In Boryeong, the fun lasts from day to night, making it the perfect place to create unforgettable summer memories.

title: Ulsan Shipbuilding & Sea Festival

title: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival

It has been named an Honorary Culture and Tourism Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and selected as a Preliminary Global Festival. Its signature event, the Salsu Battle Street Parade, turns the city streets into a giant splash zone where anyone can join in the fun. Other highlights include the World’s Largest Water Fight, Catch the Golden Fish, and a range of action-packed water activities. During the day, visitors can cool off with lively water games and activities. After sunset, the energy continues with K-pop concerts, Jangheung Water Beat, and other spectacular night performances. Programs such as the Papillon ZIP experience and Jangheung Camping Stay also invite visitors to enjoy the area’s nature, food, and local attractions. Open to visitors of all ages and backgrounds, the festival is a refreshing summer getaway where everyone can escape the everyday and dive into the fun.

title: Saturday Permanent Stage Propose and Sacheon Rock Festival
titleFull: Saturday Permanent Stage Propose and Sacheon Rock Festival (토요상설무대 프러포즈 및 사천 락 페스티벌)
overview: This summer, a special music journey called the Saturday Permanent Stage Propose will be held in Sacheon at the maritime stage of Samcheongpo Bridge Park. Every Saturday evening, various genres of artists will come against the backdrop of the beautiful sea and sunset. It is a performance where you can enjoy a midsummer night’s show with the cool sea breeze and create unforgettable memories with family, friends, and loved ones. Additionally, participation in the national proposal event "To Reach You" is also possible, and special gifts can be received.

title: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives
titleFull: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives (도기陶器, 우리를 담은 질그릇)
overview: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives is a special exhibition held at the National Gwangju Museum. By looking back at earthenware, a type of pottery which has been at the core of our daily lives for a long time, we can encounter the practicality, aesthetic sense, and the stories contained in the earthenware that has been passed down through tradition. This exhibition showcases over 300 artifacts, including a ribbed bottle and large jars excavated from the Cheonghaejin site in Wando.

title: Garden Night Market
overview: The Garden Night Market is a night market held in urban parks during the summer season. It consists of 10 sales booths, 5 experience booths, 10 food booths, and 16 food trucks, providing a variety of experiences for citizens and tourists. Play facilities and forest experiences are prepared for participants visiting with children, and colorful busking performances add to the ambiance of a summer night. Amidst the hot summer, the vibrant night market offers participants a fresh and unique experience as a nighttime themed tourist attraction.

title: Andong National Heritage Night - Wolyeong Night Stroll
titleFull: Andong National Heritage Night - Wolyeong Night Stroll (안동 국가유산 야행 월영야행)
overview: The Andong National Heritage Night "Wolyeong Night Stroll" takes place around Woryeonggyo Bridge, offering visitors the opportunity to explore Andong’s national heritage while walking under the moonlight. The program is centered on storytelling inspired by the area’s cultural heritage and is held in the vicinity of Woryeonggyo Bridge. Visitors can engage with the historical value of Andong’s heritage through a variety of themed programs, including night views, guided routes, historical storytelling, performances, markets, food offerings, exhibitions, and lodging. These activities provide multiple ways to experience the cultural significance of Andong in an immersive nighttime setting.
sponsor: National Heritage Service, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Andong City

title: Incheon Pentaport Rock Festival
titleFull: Incheon Pentaport Rock Festival (인천펜타포트 락 페스티벌)
overview: The Incheon Pentaport Music Festival is one of Korea’s premier global music events and a major fixture in the country’s rock scene. Since its launch in 2006, it has grown into one of Korea’s flagship festivals, earning recognition from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The 2026 festival will be held at Songdo Moonlight Festival Park in Incheon, featuring headline performances by top Korean and international artists along with a wide range of high-quality festival programs. Beyond the main stages, programs such as Penta Super Rookie and Live Club Party support emerging artists and help energize the local music scene. Ahead of the festival, special pre-festival shows will take place in Hongdae and Tokyo, giving fans in Korea and abroad more ways to connect with Pentaport while building anticipation for the main event. Pop-up stores will offer official merchandise and branded content, adding another layer to the festival experience. At the crossroads of music and urban culture, the festival has become a global cultural platform and a signature event that raises Incheon’s profile as a city of culture.

title: Seoul Fringe Festival
overview: Seoul Fringe Festival has been held every summer annually since 1998. The festival is open to artists of all genres, from dance to music and media art. Due to the open style and non-competitive element of the festival, artists and festival-goers alike are free to express themselves however they choose.
fee: Varies by program  * Refer to the official website for details

title: 100 Years Night Night Market
titleFull: 100 Years Night Night Market (백년나이트 야시장 (메기의 귀환))
overview: 100 Year Market, a traditional market with a long history, transforms into a vibrant night market as evening falls. With a mini mirror ball, neon signs, and a mini DJ booth alongside new dining options each month, this retro-themed market is perfect for visitors of all ages.

title: Busan Sea Festival

title: Tongyeong Hansan Battle Festival
overview: The 65th Tongyeong Hansan Battle Festival is one of Korea’s leading patriotic history and cultural festivals, commemorating the victory at the Battle of Hansan, one of the three great naval victories of the Imjin War, and honoring the spirit and leadership of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Held throughout Tongyeong around the anniversary of the victory, on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month (August 14 in 2026), the festival features programs that bring this historic event to life, including a reenactment of the Battle of Hansan, the Parade of the Three Provinces Naval Commander, the departure ceremony, and a victory homecoming ceremony. Visitors of all ages can enjoy traditional cultural experiences, performances, exhibitions, marine leisure activities, media content, and nighttime programs. Set against Tongyeong’s beautiful coastline and rich historical heritage, the festival blends tradition and modern creativity while continuing to grow as a globally recognized festival of history and patriotic remembrance.
place: Tongyeong Hansan Battle Plaza and other locations across Tongyeong

title: Gangneung National Heritage Night
titleFull: Gangneung National Heritage Night (강릉 국가유산 야행)

It promotes the active use of cultural heritage through a variety of activities such as performances, hands-on experiences, and art programs set in historically significant areas. The program encourages visitors to engage with and appreciate the meaning and value of cultural heritage, offering immersive nighttime experiences that highlight Gangneung’s history and culture through sights, food, and entertainment.
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service, Gangwon State, Gangneung City

The lineup includes healing yoga classes combining aromatherapy and tea ceremony on the Kyeryong Spatel lawn, an open-air cinema with big screen and wireless headsets, small classical and film-music concerts in the front yard of Biryongjae — a former presidential villa — and an anytime running challenge along the Gapcheon stream. Participants get coupons usable at hotels, cafes, and bakeries in the hot-spring district. Schedules and sign-up at the official site (yu-on.com).

title: Gaya Theme Park Light Festival
titleFull: Gaya Theme Park Light Festival (가야테마파크 빛 축제 빛을 향한 항해)
overview: The Gaya Theme Park Light Festival showcases the story of departure, navigation, and the encounter with Gaya through light sculptures, illuminations, media art, and photo zones. Walking along the path of light resembling the blue sea and night sky. On weekends and holidays, a local food zone, regional creator art market, and outdoor performances featuring jazz, fusion traditional music, and acoustic music will be added. Experience a special summer night in Gimhae where light, history, performances, food, and art come together.

The fair also highlights the powerful impact of illustrated works across both online and offline marketing, as well as their continued growth as an industry. Visitors can explore the latest trends in illustration and discover the diverse world of artists.

It also features interactive content and message-based content that encourage visitor participation. The exhibition period is divided into PHASE 1 and PHASE 2, with changes to some VR and hologram content as well as purchase perks. The exhibition operates on a 100% advance reservation basis with 12 sessions per day, and an MD ZONE for visitors will be available on-site.

title: 5th Jeju Biennale: The Art of Transformation

Anchored at the Jeju Museum of Art with satellite venues including the Jeju Stone Park's Obaekjanggun Gallery (free with a biennale ticket), it presents an aesthetics of survival shaped by nature, human life, and the sacred.

title: Yuseong Jazz & Beer Festa

title: Cheonan K-Culture Expo

Since its inaugural edition in 2023, the expo has been held annually for three consecutive years, integrating exhibition, performance, interactive, and consumer-oriented programs into a comprehensive cultural platform. Through ongoing collaboration with the Independence Hall, cultural and arts institutions, and regional industries, the expo continues to strengthen its operational stability while expanding its scale and scope.

This year adds a changgeuk (Korean opera) performance inside Jibokjae, King Gojong's private library, before the evening closes at Hyangwonji Pond under the stars. One of the most sought-after tickets among the palace night programs — book early.

Free, nightly 19:30–22:30.

title: Starry Sea Busan: Night Camp-nic at Dadaepo
overview: Dadaepo Beach Park — Busan's famous sunset spot — turns into an evening festival ground for three September weekends. The program runs from 'Sunset Eat-nic' picnic dining against the sunset, to the headline 'Night Music Camp-nic' of live music under camping lights, plus a dog-friendly 'Play Mung-nic' zone and wellness programs. title: Gangbuk Baengmaek Festival
overview: The Baengmaek Festival, which has grown into a representative event of Gangbuk-gu since 2023, aims to help transform Uicheon Stream into a permanent night market and a cultural space centered along the stream. In line with Seoul’s efforts to develop attractions near the stream, the festival highlights the area’s scenic waterfront as its main venue. Bringing together local businesses and young entrepreneurs, the festival creates a welcoming space for people of all ages. Rather than focusing on big-name performers, it features a variety of busking acts and performances by local artists, encouraging community participation. It also expands opportunities for small businesses by offering spaces for traditional market foods and craft beer, helping vendors reach new customers.
place: Baengnyeon Market and Uicheon Stream Area (Ssanghangyo Bridge to Uigyo Bridge) in Gangbuk-gu

title: Starry Sea Busan - Night Camp Picnic

This event is not just about enjoyment; it is composed of various programs. Visitors can enjoy delicious food against the backdrop of a beautiful sunset, experience the camping vibe with live music under the starlight, create precious memories with pets, and take part in a wellness program to invigorate tired daily lives.

title: Hongseong Namdang Port Jumbo Shrimp Festival
titleFull: Hongseong Namdang Port Jumbo Shrimp Festival (홍성남당항 대하축제)
overview: Namdang Port, located at the west end of Hongseong, is a famous west coast port known for its exceptional seafood. Surrounded by the clean waters of Cheonsuman Bay, Namdang Port is home to a wide array of sea life including blue crab, cockle and webfoot octopus. Namdang Port also draws throngs of visitors from early September to mid-October every year for the country’s largest Jumbo Shrimp Festival.

title: Hyoseok Cultural Festival
overview: The Hyoseok Cultural Festival is one of Korea’s best-known fall cultural tourism festivals, held in Bongpyeong-myeon, Pyeongchang-gun, Gangwon-do. First held in 1999, the festival takes place around September every year in Bongpyeong-myeon, the real-life setting of When the Buckwheat Flowers Bloom, a classic modern Korean short story by Lee Hyo-seok (pen name: Gasan). The festival is best known for its vast fields of white buckwheat flowers, which bloom so densely that they look as if they have been dusted with salt. Visitors can experience firsthand the natural scenery of Bongpyeong that serves as the backdrop to the story. The program includes literary events honoring Lee Hyo-seok and his work, traditional folk games, a food market featuring local specialties, and a variety of cultural and artistic performances by local residents and artists. In doing so, the festival helps promote the region’s literary heritage and rural traditions while also supporting the local economy.

title: Muju Firefly Festival
overview: The Muju Firefly Festival is one of Korea’s leading environmental festivals, themed around fireflies, a designated Natural Monument in Korea, and Muju’s pristine natural environment. Held throughout Muju-gun each year from around late August to early September, the festival offers visitors a special opportunity to see fireflies glowing in the wild and appreciate the value of nature and the importance of preserving the ecological environment. During the festival, visitors can enjoy a wide range of ecological and environmental activities, traditional cultural events, performances, and nighttime attractions. A signature highlight is the Firefly Mystery Exploration, Muju's unique program that takes visitors directly to firefly habitats to witness their magical glow in the wild. The experience leaves visitors with unforgettable memories. The Muju Firefly Festival has established itself as a celebration of the value of coexistence between people and nature, while raising awareness of the importance of environmental conservation.

It is aimed at revitalizing the local economy and promoting coexistence. Starting with an opening ceremony and celebratory performances, the festival will feature a variety of content that all generations can enjoy, including booths for Pohang 10 Taste and night market food, a food promotion hall, DJ club parties, a GOGO singing contest, a small business flea market, and a children's fire truck experience zone. It will be conducted as a clean festival using eco-friendly reusable containers, aiming to enhance the brand value of Pohang as a food city through specialized night market experiences that combine food, performances, and activities.

The day mixes a participatory play about his life, mulberry natural-dye workshops, and a hanok exploration program for children, plus a free gayageum recital.
