title: 16th Gwangju Biennale: You Must Change Your Life
overview: Asia's most established contemporary art biennale opens September 5 under a title borrowed from the last line of Rilke's 1908 poem 'Archaic Torso of Apollo' — the moment a broken ancient statue upends how the viewer sees the world. The 16th edition builds on that jolt: when your vantage point shifts, you can no longer live as before. Held at the Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall, the event anchors Korea's contemporary art calendar and pairs well with the city's May 18 memorial sites and food scene.

title: Car-Free Jamsugyo Bridge Walking Festival
overview: On festival Sundays, Seoul closes Jamsugyo — the low double-deck bridge that skims the Han River at Banpo — to traffic and hands it to pedestrians. Regular attractions include the Moonlight Diner (global street food), the Moonlight Market for crafts and eco goods, and riverside rest zones, while each edition adds rotating specials like the 'Jamsugyo Water Wars' water-gun battle and the reimagined 'Moonlight Jamsugyo'. Free, 14:00–22:00, with the Banpo Rainbow Fountain nearby — one of the most pleasant free evenings in the city.

title: Heritage Media Art at Buyeo Jeongnimsa Temple Site

Projections on the five-story stone pagoda and lecture hall, laser art, large-screen displays, AI-based interactive pieces, and kinetic sculpture draw on Sabi-era motifs: the Great Gilt-bronze Incense Burner, lotus-pattern roof tiles, Baekje astronomy, craft, and architecture. Nightly 19:00–22:00, September 7–27, free. A rare chance to see one of Korea's most austere heritage sites in a completely different register.

title: 2026 National e-Festival for Students with Disabilities

title: Deoksugung Palace: Night at Seokjojeon Hall
overview: An evening at Seokjojeon, the neoclassical Western-style hall of the Korean Empire inside Deoksugung Palace. The program pairs a guided night tour of the hall with a terrace-cafe experience — coffee (gabae, the drink Emperor Gojong loved) and dessert over live classical music — and a musical performance telling the story of the imperial household. Running since 2021 and now a twice-yearly fixture, it closes with period-prop photos to take home. Around 100 minutes per session; tickets are limited and sell fast.
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: Gumi Local Food Festa in Seoul
overview: The city of Gumi brings its farm produce and G-Food brand to Seoul Plaza for a two-day showcase: sales booths direct from farms, a city promotion hall, an agri-food export fair, hands-on programs, and a produce auction visitors can join. A chance to browse regional Korean produce without leaving downtown Seoul.

title: Red Food Festival
overview: Jangsu is known for producing some of Korea’s finest Hanu (Korean beef) and apples. Launched in 2007 with these two local specialties at its heart, the festival reaches its 20th edition in 2026, making a long and distinguished history. It also holds the distinction of being Korea’s first Red Color Festival. Since 2024, the festival has expanded its focus from Hanu and apples to a broader range of Jangsu Red Foods, including omija and tomatoes. It now also features a growing selection of processed specialties such as apple beer, apple soju, apple bread, and omija wine. Having evolved from Korea’s first Red Color Festival into the country’s first Red Food Festival, the event continues to expand its scope and enhance its standing as one of Korea’s leading cultural tourism festivals.
place: Uiam Park area, Jangsu-eup, Jangsu-gun, Jeonbuk-do
sponsor: Jangsu Red Food Festival Promotion Committee

title: 5th Horror Hologram Festival
overview: An immersive horror festival staged inside the Iksan Prison Set — the disused prison film set where many Korean movies were shot. The main event fuses hologram technology from Jeonbuk's hologram industry with escape-room mechanics and live theatrical scares, backed by stage events, quiz shows, and food stalls. Free entry, evenings 18:00–22:00 — a genuinely unusual venue even by horror-attraction standards, worth the detour for genre fans.

title: Gwangju ACE Fair
addr: 30 Sangmunuri-ro, Seo-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Held at the Kimdaejung Convention Center, the 2026 Gwangju ACE Fair is a comprehensive cultural content festival where broadcasting, animation, characters, games, and webtoons converge. This dynamic event serves as both a professional business hub for industry networking and a vibrant playground for the public. While domestic and international companies showcase the latest trends in the exhibition halls, visitors can enjoy a rich array of participatory programs, including an illustration fair featuring unique artist goods, lively cosplay competitions, and stage events with popular creators. The festival also offers family-friendly entertainment such as a dedicated board game zone and bubble shows, alongside creative markets like the Juicy Festival and Semogwi Market for exclusive character merchandise.
fee: Free with advance online booking* Refer to the official website for details
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Gwangju Metropolitan City

title: 38th Chuncheon Puppet Festival
overview: Asia's largest puppet-theater festival, drawing top puppeteers and companies from around the world to Chuncheon. Centered on the Chuncheon Puppet Theater but spilling across the city, the program spans international performances, a large-scale parade, an art market, and workshops, exhibitions, and hands-on programs that push the boundaries of the genre. Long a fixture of the world puppetry circuit, it is genuinely all-ages — as rewarding for adults as for children. Fees and times vary by program.
place: Chuncheon Puppet Theater and citywide venues

title: Daejeon Jung-gu Heritage Night Tour
overview: A night festival threading together the modern-era heritage of Daejeon's original downtown — the former Chungcheongnam-do Provincial Office, Daeheung-dong Cathedral, and other early-20th-century buildings — with light installations, storytelling, performances, hands-on programs, and a night market through the old alleys. The point is to walk, listen, and participate rather than just look, discovering a district where the city's past and present coexist. Free (some programs paid), 18:00–22:00.

title: Seoul International Writers' Festival
overview: Seoul International Writers' Festival was founded in 2006 with aims to lay a foundation for connecting Korean literature and international literature. The festival provides the opportunity to get a deeper understanding of literature through programs such as meeting Korean and international authors and participating in writers' workshop.

title: Myeongnyang Daecheop Festival
overview: A history festival commemorating the Battle of Myeongnyang (1597), when Admiral Yi Sun-sin's 13 ships defeated a vastly larger Japanese fleet in the roaring strait of Uldolmok. Jointly held by Jindo and Haenam counties on both shores of the actual strait, the festival's centerpiece is a multimedia naval-battle reenactment blending ICT effects with a marine parade, plus a departure parade, regional performances, nightscape lighting, and hands-on history programs. One of the most dramatic settings of any Korean festival — the tidal current that won the battle still races under the Jindo Bridge.
place: Uldolmok Strait (Usuyeong, Haenam and Nokjin, Jindo)

title: Namdo K-Garden Festival
overview: A 51-day night garden festival in Yeosu's old downtown under the theme 'A Night Garden Embracing Islands'. Around 40 gardens — showcase gardens, designer gardens, and citizen-made plots — line the Yeomun culture street and Yeoseo plaza, viewable day and night with evening lighting that ties into Yeosu's night-tourism circuit. Garden-interpretation walks, performances, and hands-on programs run throughout, 15:00–21:00, free. Runs September 11 to October 31, overlapping the city's peak autumn season.

title: Gwangmyeong Madanggeuk Festival
overview: A performing-arts festival devoted to madanggeuk — Korea's open-air folk theater of satire, humor, and audience participation — co-hosted with the national madanggeuk association. Now in its third year, it turns the Gwangmyeong Civic Stadium grounds into an open stage for madanggeuk, fusion gugak, circus, and street performance, with citizen-participation programs alongside. The form's defining trait is that the line between stage and audience disappears — expect to be pulled in. Free, 16:00–21:00.
sponsor: Gwangmyeong Cultural Foundation · Korea Madanggeuk Association

title: Geoje Beer Festival
overview: Geoje Island's signature autumn festival: unlimited draft beer against the night sea of Jangseungpo Port. The waterfront park fills with local food and food trucks, while the stage cycles through EDM, K-pop, and retro hits with audience events between sets. The festival also runs tourism booths, photo zones, local makgeolli tastings, a barrier-free zone, and reusable-container operations. Ticketed entry; evenings 18:00–22:00.

title: Moonlight Music Festival
overview: The Moonlight Music Festival is a cultural and arts performance series designed to let people enjoy music on autumn nights from September through October in familiar, everyday settings across Daejeon’s five districts. As an open-air event free to all citizens, it will feature a total of five performances—one in each district. Against the backdrop of cool autumn nights, local artists performing a variety of genres will take the stage, alongside performances by popular singers. By adding music to the familiar and comfortable parks and riversides in the city center, the Moonlight Music Festival aims to provide special moments and experiences where families, couples, and friends can enjoy music together and share the joy of live performances as part of their daily lives.
place: Areas of Gapcheon Ecological Lake Park, Eungubi Park, Urideul Park, Dongchundang Park, Daedongcheon Stream

title: Dalseong Daegu Contemporary Art Festival
overview: An open-air contemporary art festival at Gangjeong, by the sculptural ARC building on the Nakdong River. It inherits the spirit of the 1970s Daegu Contemporary Art Festival, when young artists challenged the rigidity of the art establishment — the 1977 edition at this very riverside drew some 200 artists in what is considered Korea's first collective art event. Free, open 11:00–22:00, and easy to combine with a riverside bike ride out of Daegu.

title: Seocheon Heritage Night Tour
overview: A two-night heritage festival at Hansan Eupseong Fortress in Seocheon, themed 'The Lord of Hansan's Rowdy Incognito Outing'. The old fortress town — home of Korea's famous Hansan ramie fabric — hosts night performances, hands-on programs, and exhibitions that blend tradition with contemporary staging, September 11–12, 18:00–22:00, free. Part of Korea's national 'Heritage Night' series, which opens heritage sites after dark with food, light, and stories.

title: GXG 2026
overview: Korea's largest urban game-culture festival, held in Pangyo — the Silicon Valley of the Korean game industry. GXG (Game culture X Generation) treats games as culture rather than just play: the main program is GXG SOUND TRACK, a game-music competition, surrounded by concerts, exhibitions, and experience zones covering game music, video, and art. Free, on the plaza around Pangyo Station, 13:00–22:00 — an easy subway ride from Gangnam and a good window into Korean gaming culture.

title: Chuncheon Sul Festa
overview: Chuncheon's traditional-liquor and local-food festival, celebrating the city's brewing culture. Local breweries pour takju, distilled soju, yakju, fruit wines, and craft beer for tasting, with bottles sold at fair prices, while local food brands and food trucks supply pairings. A busking stage and hands-on programs round out the evening at KT&G Sangsangmadang Chuncheon. Free entry; drinks purchased on site. An easy add-on to a Chuncheon day trip from Seoul on the ITX line.

title: Cheongsong White Porcelain Festival
overview: Cheongsong baekja — white porcelain fired here for 500 years from local clay, water, and fire — gets its own festival at the pottery village near Juwangsan National Park. Under the slogan '500 years of history, 500 years of future', the festival mixes exhibitions, sales, wheel-throwing and other hands-on programs, and cultural performances that trace the craft's past and hand it to the next generation. Free entry (some workshops paid), 10:00–19:00. Combine with Juwangsan's rock spires — this is one of Korea's quietest, prettiest counties.

title: Sinchon Global University Culture Festival
overview: Sinchon — Seoul's classic university district — fills Yonsei-ro with a festival built on its two identities: global culture and student culture. University students plan and run much of the program themselves: global culture-experience booths, world food stalls, and student-culture booths line the street, while the main stage cycles through student performances, global acts, and participatory events. Free, 11:00–21:00, and one of the easiest places to feel Korean campus energy without an invitation.

title: Muchangpo Mystic Sea Road Festival
overview: Twice a month, the tide at Muchangpo Beach pulls back to expose a 1.5km sea road — and this Boryeong festival is timed to it. By day, walk the tidal flats when the sea parts, catch fish bare-handed, and watch open-air madanggeuk theater; after dark, the signature LED torch walk sends a line of lights out across the exposed seabed. A rare festival where the main event is a natural phenomenon, with the schedule set by the tide tables. Free entry; some programs paid.

title: Samto Festival
overview: Wonju's harvest-season celebration of farming and rural culture. A direct farm market sells the region's produce at source prices, family programs cover rural crafts and games, and local arts groups fill the stage across the day. Less a tourist spectacle than a genuine regional fair — which is exactly its charm if you want to see how a Korean provincial city celebrates its farming roots. Free, 10:00–21:00 at the Wonju sports complex.

title: Paju K-Culture Festival
overview: A K-culture festival at the former Paju English Village — now a shooting location for K-pop survival shows, music videos, and K-dramas. The program brings K-pop and cover-dance performances together with K-food, traditional Korean games, and around 30 hands-on K-culture booths, plus four-cut photo studios, stamp events, and traditional costume try-ons. Free, 10:00–17:00. For K-content fans, the venue itself — a purpose-built European-style village an hour from Seoul — is half the draw.
place: Gyeonggi Future Education Paju Campus (former Paju English Village)

title: Cheoinseong Fortress Culture Festival
overview: In 1232, at the small earthen fortress of Cheoinseong, the monk-commander Kim Yun-hu and local villagers repelled the second Mongol invasion — killing the Mongol general Sartai in one of the great upsets of the era. Yongin's 35th festival in their honor stages a musical of the battle, mounted martial-arts shows, horseback riding, Goryeo costume try-ons, pottery and craft workshops, and guided history walks, closing with night performances and fireworks. Free entry, 10:00–22:00, with food trucks on site. A linked mission event connects it to October's Poeun Culture Festival.

title: Daejeon Jung-gu Book Festival
titleFull: Daejeon Jung-gu Book Festival (대전 중구 북페스티벌)
overview: The Jung-gu Book Festival builds on the diverse reading cultures and voices discovered within Jung-gu, bringing them together to foster new connections throughout the district. Presenting the district as a place shaped by layers of stories accumulated over time, the festival traces the time embedded in its alleys, the memories preserved in the old downtown, the lives of its people, and the emotions held by the community. In doing so, it uncovers and connects the stories that already exist within Jung-gu in a different perspective.
fee: Free admission (certain programs may require a participation fee of 1,000 won to 5,000 won)

title: Colorful Garden: Jaraseom Flower Festa
overview: Autumn flower fields blanket Jaraseom — the river island in Gapyeong best known for its jazz festival — from September 12 to October 5. Weekends add busking and local performances, plus balloon art and family programs, farm-produce booths, and snack stalls. Of the 7,000 won ticket, 5,000 won comes back as local currency to spend at booths and in town cafes and restaurants. Boats cruise the Bukhangang riverfront and an electric shuttle covers the walk in. Ticket holders get discounts at nearby attractions; Gapyeong residents enter free.
fee: 7,000 won (5,000 won returned as local currency)

title: Pyeongtaek Lake Light Festival
overview: Pyeongtaek's signature festival on the shores of Pyeongtaek Lake, built around the twin themes of water and light. The day runs family performances, hands-on programs, and food zones through the lakeside tourist complex; after dark the sky fills with the festival's headline fireworks show over the water. Local residents and artists carry much of the stage program, making it a friendly, low-key alternative to the megafestivals. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Yangju Heritage Night Tour
overview: The old government seat of Yangju-mok comes alive after dark under the theme 'Officials and people rejoicing together again'. The festival stages Yangju's remarkable roster of intangible heritage — the Byeolsandae mask dance, Sonori shamanic ox play, farming songs, and funeral bier songs — alongside a state-exam reenactment, traditional crafts, night walks, media exhibitions, and an old-style market with teahouse. Programs follow the classic '8 nights' structure of Korea's Heritage Night series (night views, night roads, night stories and more). Free, 17:00–22:00.

title: Jeju Leisure Healing Festival
overview: Two days of leisure sports and wellness on Hamdeok Beach, one of Jeju's most beautiful white-sand bays. Headline concerts each evening (past lineups have drawn major Korean acts) bookend a daytime program of paddleboarding, flying disc, and trail running, balanced by wellness content: morning yoga on the sand, stargazing nights, and sketch-drawing sessions overlooking the water. Opens with a beach party performance and closes with a water-splash finale. Free, 07:00–22:00.

title: Seoul Intangible Heritage Festival
overview: Seoul's intangible-heritage traditions gather in Namsangol Hanok Village for a weekend of performances, exhibitions, demonstrations, and tastings, organized into five themed courtyards: a spirited performance stage, a craft court where master artisans work within arm's reach, a taste court of traditional food and drink, an open participation court, and a heritage-collecting trail. Set among the village's relocated hanok houses under Namsan, it is one of the best-value traditional culture days in the city. Free (some programs paid).

title: Pocheon Hantangang Garden Festa
overview: A large-scale garden-and-ecology festival at the Hantangang Eco Landscape Complex, inside the UNESCO Global Geopark of the Hantan River gorge. Seasonal flower fields spread beneath the park's 410m Y-shaped suspension bridge, with themed designer gardens, a Pororo-themed autumn camping photo zone, a river market of Pocheon farm produce and street food, and family e-bike rides along the gorge. Ticketed entry, 09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00). The geology alone — basalt cliffs carved by ancient lava — is worth the trip from Seoul.

title: Dongdaemun-gu Book Festival
overview: A reading festival for Korea's September 'Month of Reading', themed 'Open the book, move the body!'. The plaza at the Dongdaemun-gu Office hosts reading fitness sessions, folk tales turned into physical games, and an open-air library, while the auditorium runs library-network booths from a reading adventure squad to a mini sports day and a 'reading health check'. Children's musicals, a bubble show, and busking round it out. Free, aimed squarely at families, 12:00–17:00.
place: Dongdaemun-gu Office Future Plaza and auditorium

title: 2026 DMZ Peace Festa
overview: A relay festival linking the tourism assets of the DMZ border region, long split between separate counties, into one program — this edition connecting Ganghwa Island and Cheorwon. Both legs build hands-on programs around three shared themes: nature and ecology, the lives and stories of border residents, and reflection and healing. Venues include the Hwagae Garden on Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and the history park in Cheorwon. Free; some programs need advance booking via the official site.
place: Hwagae Garden, Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and History Park (Cheorwon)
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Nowon Craft Beer Festival
overview: Thirty-four breweries from across Korea pour some 200 craft beers along the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail at Hwarangdae Railroad Park — a disused rail line turned linear park in northeast Seoul. Traditional-market vendors and food trucks handle the pairings, while the stage hosts Korean and international acts in tandem with Seoul Music Week, plus experimental student art and children's programs. Free entry; pay per pour. One of the city's best-value beer events, in an unusually atmospheric venue.

title: Wanju Sanggwan Water Pool Party
overview: A stay-style festival in Sanggwan, a valley township of Wanju county, linking its water, forests, hot springs, lodging, and food into one program. The daytime pool party and evening night market anchor the schedule, joined by cypress-forest activities ('Forest-tivity'), village and forest trekking walks, and lodging-linked stay packages. Free entry; the pool party and some programs are ticketed. Runs 10:00–22:00 at the Boem Spa & Resort area — an easy pairing with Jeonju, twenty minutes away.
fee: Free entry (pool party and some programs paid)
sponsor: Wanju County · Wanju Culture and Tourism Foundation

title: Glocal Culture in Namsan Festival
overview: A one-day neighborhood festival in Busan's Geumjeong district where global and local culture meet — powered by the international students of Busan University of Foreign Studies and the residents of Namsan-dong. The glocal food market serves fermented dishes made by the community fermentation school alongside local staples, with a flea market of local sellers and an evening citizens' concert. Namsan-ro becomes a cultural street for the day, 15:00–22:00, free.

title: 14th Busan International Port Conference
overview: The annual international conference of Busan Port — one of the world's busiest container hubs — gathering global port, shipping, and logistics leaders to share container-market outlooks and operating strategy. The 2026 agenda centers on the industry's defining shifts: digital transformation, decarbonization, and supply-chain realignment. Held at the Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center; free registration, with session times to be announced. An industry event rather than a festival — of interest mainly to maritime professionals.
place: Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center

title: Seoul Architecture Festival
overview:
The Architecture Festival aims to rediscover the unique architectural and urban charms of Seoul together with its citizens. Seoul generates creative potential based on “complex density”—a fusion of history, culture, and regional identity characteristic of a high-density city. Furthermore, amid rapid social change, the city has continuously adapted through “accelerated evolution,” which involves rapidly renewing its form based on its accumulated heritage. Moreover, through “glocality”—the intersection of local context and global trends—Seoul is expanding the unique urban experiences and values of contemporary K-architecture to the world.
The festival features a variety of participatory programs designed to allow citizens to experience Seoul’s architecture and urban landscape up close and engage with architectural culture in an accessible way. Through a diverse range of citizen-participatory content, the festival aims to create a space where citizens can discover Seoul’s architecture together and help shape K-Architecture culture.
place: Seoul Urban Architecture Exhibition Hall, B3, Bium Hall

title: Literature Week 2026: Sideways Glance
overview: Korea's national literature festival, held every year since 2016 to widen the audience for Korean writing. The 2026 edition, themed 'Sideways Glance', looks at literature and everything just outside it, over five days of readings, talks, and programs around Marronnier Park in Daehangno — Seoul's theater district. Free; program times vary. Most events are in Korean, but the park itself buzzes for the week.

title: 8th Daejeon Special Visual Effects Film Festival
overview: Korea's only film festival dedicated to VFX and special visual effects, built on Daejeon's visual-effects industry base. The program spans the DFX OTT Awards honoring effects work in Korean streaming content, DFX Screenings with director and cast talks, a DFX Tech Show on AI and VFX production trends, and DFX Pitch, which scouts feature-length effects-driven projects. Screenings spread across the DCC convention center and the city's independent cinemas. Free.

title: 2026 Gyeongbuk K-Story Festival
overview: A content-industry festival in Andong themed 'K-Story, where content begins', connecting the region's history and its creators' stories to webtoons, video, performance, and publishing. The program spans story-IP pitching sessions that link creators with buyers, keynote lectures and conferences, family experience zones, and exhibitions and performances at the Andong Culture & Arts Center. Free, 11:00–20:00 — and Andong itself, Korea's Confucian heartland and home of Hahoe Village, rewards the trip.

title: 39th Donghae Mureung Festival
overview: Donghae's flagship traditional festival, four days at the Wellbeing Leports Town under the theme 'Citizens as one, Donghae leaping anew'. It opens with mountain-spirit and harvest rites, then runs generation-spanning concerts, a citizens' song contest, youth dance festival, navy band and honor-guard shows, special-forces martial-arts demonstrations, and folk performances including Mangsang nongak and the local bridge-treading play. Family zones cover folk games, craft workshops, and children's programs; a local-restaurant tasting vote and lantern-lit night tunnel round out the grounds. Free.

title: 9th Jeonju International Short Film Festival
overview: A short-film festival in Jeonju's cinema street under the slogan 'New Frame, New Longtake' — this year expanding into vertical films shot for the phone screen while doubling down on short-form experimentation. The program combines screenings, audience talks with filmmakers, and a vertical-cinema forum at CGV Jeonju Gosa, in the heart of the city famous for its hanok village and food.

title: Eumseong Masterpiece Festival
overview: A farm-produce festival in Eumseong County, Chungbuk, showcasing and selling the region's agricultural goods and specialties. Expect produce exhibitions and direct sales, food booths, hands-on programs using local crops, and cultural performances — with growers and shoppers meeting face to face. A straightforward, local-flavored county fair rather than a tourist production.

title: Aragaya Culture Festival
overview: Haman's festival of Aragaya — the ancient Gaya confederacy kingdom whose royal tombs crown the UNESCO-listed Marisan mounds. Reenactments bring the kingdom to life: a royal procession, gate-guard changing ceremony, and mounted-warrior experiences, alongside history trails, youth-produced performances, and a fireworks-backed theme show, 'Ara Red Lotus'. Held at the Haman Museum and tomb park, 09:00–21:00, free — one of the best windows into Korea's less-told Gaya history.

title: Seoul Autumn Festa Opening
overview: The opening night of Seoul Autumn Festa — the city's 73-day performing-arts season running September 18 to November 29, when roughly 260 theater, dance, music, and traditional-arts productions play across the city. The kickoff concert at the Ttukseom Hangang Park riverside stage doubles as Seoul's declaration of itself as a performing-arts city. Free, 19:00–21:00, on the river as the season's first cool evenings arrive.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government · Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Mullae Arts Festival
overview: Mullae-dong is Seoul's strangest cultural ecosystem: precision metal workshops and artists' studios sharing the same alleys. Its festival opens that world up through three programs — 'Mullae Hyperlink' exhibitions linking the district's galleries, open studios where artists show work and process in place, and a street festival of performances, media facades, DJ sets, and markets in the alleys between lathes. Some programs need advance sign-up via the Yeongdeungpo foundation site. 12:00–19:00.

title: GES 2026: Game & Esports Seoul
overview: A global game and esports festival at Dongdaemun Design Plaza, hosted by the Seoul city government. Around 100 game and esports companies exhibit across indie and major-studio showcases, with esports tournaments (including a PUBG club match and the Seoul Cup), competitions, and networking programs drawing some 20,000 visitors. Free entry, 10:00–18:00 — three days of Korean gaming culture in one landmark venue.

title: Jinan Red Ginseng Festival
overview:
Held in Jinan-gun, Korea’s only designated red ginseng special zone, the Jinan Red Ginseng Festival is a signature fall event where visitors can enjoy both healthy local specialties and festive fun. Jinan red ginseng, known for its rich aroma and high quality, can be sampled throughout the festival, alongside a variety of unique foods and hands-on activities that make red ginseng more approachable and enjoyable for visitors of all ages.
 Highlights include Red Ginseng Bingo, Red Ginseng Power Zone, Red Ginseng Barbecue, and an Outdoor Foot Bath Experience, as well as plenty of unique interactive programs found only at the festival. Traditional performances, guest singer concerts, and a variety of stage events add to the lively atmosphere. Visitors can also shop for Jinan red ginseng products certified under strict quality standards at reasonable prices. With healthy local foods, unique experiences, and plenty of entertainment, the festival offers a memorable way to enjoy fall in Jinan.

title: Bucheon International Comics Festival
overview: Celebrating its 29th edition in 2026, the Bucheon International Comics Festival (BICOF) is one of Korea’s leading cultural tourism festivals devoted to comics and webtoons, offering something for everyone who loves the medium. This year’s festival, held under the theme “Comics & Webtoons: Easy to Love, Endless to Enjoy,” features a wide range of comic-related programs and cultural experiences designed to make the event more engaging and enjoyable for visitors. Highlights include curated and special exhibitions, meet-the-artist sessions for comics fans, the BICOF Playground and outdoor market booths offering a variety of hands-on experiences, and the International Cosplay Championship, which brings together cosplayers from 14 countries around the world.
place: Korea Manhwa Museum and Korea Manhwa Contents Agency area

title: 67th Korean Folk Arts Festival
overview: Korea's longest-running festival, held since 1958 to preserve and pass on regional folk performing arts — the event that historically surfaced many of the country's now-designated heritage traditions. The 67th edition gathers folk troupes from every province in Pyeongchang, the 2018 Winter Olympics host, for open-air performances at the Jinbu sports park. Free, 09:00–18:00: two days of farmers' music, mask dance, ritual, and song you will rarely see assembled in one place.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gangwon · Pyeongchang

title: Korea Youth Day Festival
overview: The 10th anniversary edition of Korea's official Youth Day festival, held on Gwangalli Beach in Busan. What began as an advocacy event became a legal commemoration day (third Saturday of September) in 2020, and the festival now spans youth policy, culture, careers, and entertainment: a K-pop concert, a college song contest, gala concert, youth film awards, the Korea cheerleading championship, and creator awards, all against the Gwangan Bridge backdrop. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Gamaksan Flower & Star Journey
overview: On the summit hill of Gamaksan in Geochang — the 'Star Wind Hill' — autumn wildflower fields bloom against one of southern Korea's best night skies. The sixth festival, themed 'a purple comma just for me', runs busking and sunset-hill concerts, a chrysanthemum-field walk, photo zones, a stamp tour, and a slow mailbox that delivers your letter before next year's festival. Local food tents serve bibimbap, gukbap, and jeon at village prices. Access by shuttle bus (3,000 won) or pre-booked private car.

title: Busan International Performing Arts Festival (BPAF)
overview: A street performing-arts festival along the Oncheoncheon stream and the university district near Pusan National University, staging everyday urban space as theater. The 2026 theme, 'MOSAIC: many pieces, one picture', brings 28 selected Korean and international productions to outdoor stages, joined by participatory side programs and an art market. Free, 13:00–20:00 — catch it while browsing one of Busan's liveliest student quarters.
place: Oncheoncheon stream and PNU university street

title: Gwacheon Performing Arts Festival (GPAF)
overview: Korea's first street-theater festival, running since 1997 and now drawing over 100,000 visitors each September. International and Korean companies stage outdoor and street productions across the plazas of Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, in a program mixing invited international works, Korean premieres, and commissioned pieces. Free and deliberately accessible — this is where Korean street theater made its name. 12:00–22:00.
place: Gwacheon Government Complex plaza and Citizens Hall area

title: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food Festival
overview: A festival built around Pyeongchang Dunjeonpyeong nongak — the region's designated intangible-heritage farmers' music — in the highland township of Yongpyeong. The drumming and dance performances anchor a thoroughly edible program: pot-barbecue and skewer grilling, market-style gukbap stew, and other mountain-village food, plus folk games, madanggeuk theater, and hands-on traditions. Free entry (food paid), 10:00–20:00. As unpretentious and warm as festivals get.
place: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food festival grounds

title: Yeonggwang Bulgapsan Red Spider Lily Festival
overview: Every September, millions of crimson spider lilies (sangsahwa) carpet the valley below Bulgapsa, a thousand-year-old temple on Bulgapsan Mountain. The 26th festival threads performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs along the flower paths, with soft night lighting turning the fields into a second, quieter spectacle after dark. The flower — whose leaves and blossoms never meet — symbolizes impossible love, giving the walk its bittersweet undertone. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Siheung Gaetgol Festival
overview: The Siheung Gaetgol Festival is an eco-festival held at Siheung Gaetgol Eco Park, the only inland tidal creek in Gyeonggi-do. Surrounded by wetlands and former salt fields, the festival offers a variety of ways to relax, learn, and have fun in nature. To help protect the park’s natural environment, it is held as a car-free event. A signature program is the salt-pan performance, "Memories of Salt, Dance of Water." Other performances include Concert in Gaetgol, Salt Warehouse Puppet Theater, Forest Music Festival, and the Gaetgol Senior Runway. Visitors can also enjoy a wide range of activities, including a Fantasy Hot-Air Balloon Experience, Gaetgol Adventure, Salt Play & Barefoot Salt Trail, SEA POOL Party, Insect Exploration Experience, Gaetgol Is My Playground for the Day, Salt Farm Experience, Slow Post Office, “Walk Siheung” Walking Festival, Siheung Salt Farm Ritual, Street Arts Festival, Gaetgol National Art Competition, Gaetgol Retro Photo Studio, and the Gaetgol Stamp Rally.

title: Suseongmot Festival
overview: Daegu's lakeside arts festival at Suseongmot, the city's favorite evening hangout — twice ranked the city's best regional festival. The program floats between land and water: K-arts fantasy stages of Korean orchestral music, song, and dance, an on-the-water concert and 'wave' dance performance, street arts, a citywide youth dance competition, school music showcases, and an intangible-heritage stage. Music fireworks shows bookend the festival. Free, 13:00–22:00.

title: Ocean Village
overview: A local market event on the Jangseungpo waterfront in Geoje, gathering the island's fresh farm and sea produce, small-batch foods from local makers, lifestyle goods, family items, street food, and hands-on programs in one strollable seaside venue. Runs Friday–Saturday 11:00–20:00 and Sunday to 18:00. A good graze-and-browse stop if you are touring Geoje's coast.

title: Peace Nuri Picnic Festival
overview: An autumn picnic-and-concert festival on the great lawns of Imjingak Pyeonghwa Nuri (Peace Park) near the DMZ in Paju. Spread a mat under open sky for the Peace special stage and live sets by popular Korean artists spanning generations — daytime picnicking rolling into evening concerts. Entry is a token 3,000 won. The venue itself, wind-turbine hills within sight of the border, is among Korea's most evocative concert settings.

title: 11th Ulju Mountain Film Festival
overview: Asia's leading mountain-film festival, set at the welcome center of the Yeongnam Alps — the ridge country above Ulsan. The program spotlights how humans live with nature: trial and triumph, challenge and failure, conflict and coexistence, through international mountain films and documentaries that stretch the genre's boundaries. True to its setting, screenings include open-air bivouac and car-camping sessions running to midnight. Individual screenings 3,000 won; day pass 12,000 won.
fee: Screenings 3,000 won · Day ticket 12,000 won · UMFF pass 15,000 won · Bivouac screening 10,000 won

title: Gyeonggi Ceramics Biennale
overview: The Gyeonggi Ceramics Biennale features a range of exhibitions and educational events. The event takes place at various locations in Korea famous for ceramics, including Icheon, Yeoju, and Gwangju.

title: Suwon Jazz Festival
overview: An evening of jazz on the shores of Gwanggyo Lake Park — regularly ranked among Korea's best urban landscapes. Korean and international artists cover the spectrum from straight-ahead jazz to blues and funky crossover, aimed as much at casual listeners as aficionados. Free, outdoors, 17:30–21:30: bring a mat and settle in as the lake lights come on.

title: Anyang Dance Festival
overview: Anyang's citizen festival since 2000, drawing some 300,000 visitors a year and now one of Gyeonggi Province's flagship events. Under the slogan 'Walk, run, dance!', it treats any free movement of the body as dance, filling Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park with citizen performance teams, professional stages, and open dance floors over three days. Billed as Korea's only regional K-dance festival — and defiantly participatory: you will be invited to join.
place: Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park

title: Namhansanseong Culture Festival
overview: Three days marking the 400th anniversary of the fortress walls of Namhansanseong — the UNESCO-listed mountain fortress where a Joseon king withstood siege in 1636. Gwangju City's flagship festival mixes traditional and contemporary stage performances with history experience programs, participatory events, and a hands-on art market inside the provincial park. Free; the fortress wall walk itself, ringed with autumn forest, is reason enough to come.

title: Korean Confucian Culture Festival
overview: A festival translating Confucian values — loyalty, filial piety, propriety — into contemporary life, at the Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute in Nonsan, the heartland of Joseon's Confucian academies. Three days of performances, exhibitions, a humanities book concert, the K-Confucianism international forum, and family competitions and hands-on programs. Free entry (some programs paid). Pairs naturally with nearby Donam Seowon, a UNESCO World Heritage academy.
place: Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute and Noseong-myeon area

title: Youth Coffee Festival
overview: A coffee-and-culture festival on the plazas beneath Lotte World Tower, themed 'the perfect blend to wake today's me'. Korean and international coffee and dessert brands pour tastings, surrounded by photo zones and participatory programs, while the stage runs artist performances, youth talk concerts, auditions, classic screenings, and the 29-second film festival awards. Free, 13:00–18:00 — a caffeinated afternoon in Jamsil aimed at Seoul's twenty-somethings but open to all.
place: Lotte World Tower Arena Plaza and lawn

title: Ulju Drone Festival
overview: A day of drones at Jakcheonjeong plaza in Ulju: balloon-popping and obstacle-racing drone games, drone basketball, plus AI baduk robots, an AI painter, quadruped robots, 3D printing, and a disaster-safety experience hall. Stages feature Chae Yeon, Lee Ji-hoon, Sleepy, and local crews. The finale is the point: a 1,300-drone light show choreographed to music over the autumn night sky — one of the larger drone shows on the Korean festival circuit. Free, 14:00–21:00.

title: Alien Festival
overview: Korea's only alien-themed festival, run by the Miryang Arirang Space Observatory — the country's observatory specializing in the search for extraterrestrial life. The 7th edition is styled as an 'alien sports day': Meteor Run races, laser tag, and a costume contest get families running rather than watching, with space-science content woven through for the educational payoff. Free, 10:00–18:00 at the Miryang stadium grounds.

title: Mungyeong Eco-Camping Festival
overview: Camping, environment, and music meet on the banks of the Yeonggang River in Mungyeong. The program pairs the Yeonggang River Run with upcycling and recycling workshops that make resource circulation hands-on, plus family side events through the day. The closer is a headline hip-hop double bill — Dynamic Duo and Mighty Mouth — heating up the riverside autumn night. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Gwangmyeong Book Festival
overview: Gwangmyeong's reading-culture festival on the lawn of the civic gymnasium, slogan: 'The start of infinite exploration, a friendly book journey!'. The grounds fill with hands-on programs, performances, author book concerts, and all-ages reading events designed to make books a shared outing rather than a solitary habit. Free, 10:00–17:00; program details on the city library website.

title: Ansan Daebu Grape Festival
overview: Daebudo Island's sea-breeze vineyards produce unusually sweet, aromatic grapes, and this festival — running since 1995 — is their annual showcase. A direct-sale market cuts out the middleman for freshly picked bunches, while the signature grape-stomping event, concerts, the Daebu Haesol-gil walking festival, and the Ansan marathon fill the weekend at the Daebu Sea Fragrance Theme Park. Free, 09:00–18:00; an easy island day trip on Seoul's doorstep.

title: Seoul Philharmonic Park Concert
overview: The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra under music director Jaap van Zweden plays a free open-air evening at the Forest Stage of Seoul Children's Grand Park, joined by top-flight guest soloists. No reservation needed — just arrive and sit — and the concert streams live on the Seoul city and orchestra YouTube channels. 19:00–20:30. One of the easiest ways to hear a world-class orchestra for free.
place: Forest Stage, Seoul Children's Grand Park

title: Tuntun Pet Festa
overview: A two-day pet festival at Dongtan Yeoul Park in Hwaseong — a park already built for dogs, with its own pet playground. The fifth edition runs craft programs (walk bottle-bags, photo mugs), plus practical counseling corners: pet legal advice, health-check consultations, and behavior consultations, backed by the agriculture ministry and the Korea Kennel Association. Free entry, 10:00–18:00; bring the dog.

title: Suwon Hwaseong Media Art
overview:
Suwon Hwaseong Media Art is a nighttime festival held against the backdrop of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Since its launch in 2021, the event has presented large-scale media art inspired by the fortress and its history. Beginning in 2026, the festival has been newly reimagined under the theme “Saebit Dongrak: Suwon Hwaseong Blossoming in Light,” inviting visitors to experience the site through light and shared enjoyment.

The festival brings together light, video, and performance to create immersive media art installations that trace the stories of people from the construction of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress to the present. Centered around the Hwahongmun Gate and Jangan Park areas, it features a wide range of experiential and interactive works, offering visitors a dynamic mix of visual spectacles and engaging activities throughout the event period.
place: Area of Hwaseomun Gate, Janganmun Gate, and Jangan Park

title: Seokgye Station Moonlight Night Market
overview: A neighborhood night market at the culture park by Seokgye Station in northeast Seoul, run to boost the local alley economy. Food booths, craft beer and makgeolli, retro games, photo zones, and a flea market fill the park, with busking stages and headline performances (past editions have drawn well-known Korean singers). Booth prices vary; open 14:00–22:00. A low-key, genuinely local slice of Seoul night-market culture.

title: Bibliotheca Busan
overview: Bibliotheca Busan, set against the stunning backdrop of the sea in Busan, is an outdoor festival that blends books, culture, and art. Visitors can enjoy reading as well as cultural programs organized in collaboration with public libraries, bookstores, publishers, and cultural institutions in Busan.
hours: 14:00-21:00* Subject to change depending on weather conditions

title: Gyeongju Golden Carnival
overview: A music festival with no main stage. Under the concept 'OFF THE STAGE', Gyeongju's old downtown — a shuttered cinema, empty storefronts, cafes, and alleys around the Hwangnidan and Geumnidan streets — becomes a constellation of small live venues, and the audience discovers performances rather than arriving at them. Local food and drink pace the wandering between sets. A one-ticket (55,000 won) experiment in using an ancient city's modern quarter as an instrument. 11:00–22:00.

title: Seoul Street Arts Festival
overview: Seoul Street Arts Festival is held in Ttukseom Hangang Park and Seoul Forest. This year's festival presents international performances from France, Lithuania, Chile and more, in addition to local performances.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government, Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Han River Walk
overview: The Han River Walk is a walking event that takes place at various locations along the Hangang River. Participants can expect to enjoy light exercise in beautiful natural settings, as well as earn a completion medal. In addition to walking, the festival dates will feature a range of additional events for a lively environment.

title: Gijang Pet Culture Festival
overview: A companion-animal festival in Busan's Gijang County themed 'happy coexistence with pets' — its third edition. New this year: a walk-together event for pets and owners, and 'K-Pet Got Talent', a national showcase for gifted dogs and cats. Experience, education, and participation programs run throughout, aimed at both pet owners and the pet-curious, with responsible pet culture and animal welfare as the through-line. Free, 09:00–18:00 at Jeonggwan Central Park.

title: Incheon Reading Festival
overview: Incheon's book festival at the Incheon Art Platform — a cluster of restored early-1900s port warehouses in the open-port district. Under the slogan 'Read Incheon, connect hearts', the outdoor plaza hosts picture-book performances, busking, a book market of local bookstores and publishers, photo zones, and a book-themed escape game, while indoor sessions run author meetings, book talks, and forums. Free, 11:00–17:00 — and the surrounding Incheon open-port streets and Chinatown make a full day of it.

title: Seoripul Music Festival
overview: For one weekend a year, Seoul closes the ten-lane Banpo-daero boulevard and turns it into a concert ground — the signature move of this Seocho district festival, which has drawn a cumulative 1.34 million visitors since 2015. The 2026 edition, 'Seocho is the Music', caps a month-long borough-wide music journey with two days of multi-genre stages and citizen programs on the open avenue. Free (market and food booths excepted).

title: Uiwang Baekun Lake Festival
overview: Uiwang's autumn festival on the lawn plaza of Baekun Lake, a reservoir ringed by wooded hills just south of Seoul. Headline music performances share the bill with busking, free and paid hands-on programs, food courts, and events by local artists and residents — a community festival first, with the lake path there for strolling between acts. Free, 10:00–22:00.

title: Suwon Nammun Market Night Market 'Bulchwimugwi'
overview: 'No going home sober!' — King Jeongjo's famous toast lends its name to this night market at the Paldalmun gate markets in Suwon, held September 5 and 19. Built on the history of the market Jeongjo opened for his people, it fills the streets with food trucks, merchant stalls, and an art market, wrapped in a light story-world: duel the wandering taoist character, hunt hidden talismans, break magical seals. Eat, walk, and photograph your way through a market district that has been trading since the 18th century.
place: Paldalmun plaza and Jidonggyo Bridge area

title: Haksan Madanggeuk Nollae Festival
overview: A citizen-created theater festival in Incheon's Michuhol district, running since 2014. Residents write and stage their own madanggeuk — open-air folk theater — drawing on neighborhood issues and life stories, in forms ranging from percussion drama and mask dance to puppet, music, and staged-reading theater. Performed outdoors by the artificial waterfall in Subong Park, it is community art in the most literal sense: the neighbors are the cast. Free, 17:00–21:00.

title: Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo
overview: Goseong is one of the world's three great dinosaur-footprint fossil sites, and its expo — running since 2006, now in its 10th edition and 20th year — is Korea's flagship dinosaur event. The Danghangpo venue combines a dinosaur theme zone and an Admiral Yi Sun-sin zone with coastal walks, trails, and fossil-footprint paths. The 2026 theme is 'an exciting adventure with dinosaurs', with exhibitions, hands-on programs, and shows aimed squarely at families. Adults 19,000 won, children 13,000 won; open to 22:00 on night-opening days.

title: Andong Maskdance Festival
overview: The Andong Maskdance Festival is a global celebration where the memories carried by masks come to life through dance. Visitors can experience Korea’s mask dance traditions, inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list, alongside mask dances from around the world. A wide range of performances, parades, the Tallori Daedongnanjang community celebrations, and the World Maskplay Competition create opportunities for people to come together and share in the festival experience. The 2026 Andong Maskdance Festival seeks to connect the stories preserved in masks with contemporary life. As children and seniors, local residents and international visitors gather in the same place to laugh, applaud, and share the rhythm of the festival, the memories carried by masks become a living culture. Shaped by the participation of all who take part, the festival becomes a true “dance for everyone,” celebrating the power of community and the joy of coming together.
place: Jungang Line 1942 Andong Station, Mask Dance Park, and Andong Old Downtown
sponsor: Korea Foundation for Cultures and Ethics

title: Changgyeonggung Palace Night Banquet
overview: A family-friendly night banquet at Changgyeonggung Palace, reinterpreting the feast Crown Prince Hyomyeong held for his father King Sunjo. Participants dress in court attire as Joseon officials and noblewomen, taste royal confections, watch traditional performances, and join palace experience programs around Munjeongjeon Hall. The autumn run spans late September through early October — including the Chuseok holiday — making it a natural family outing for the season. Sessions 17:00–20:30.
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: 2026 Korea Urban & Regional Innovation Expo
overview: Korea's largest urban-innovation expo, gathering government ministries, local governments, and companies around urban regeneration and regional innovation — exhibitions, seminars, and results-sharing sessions across four days at Osong Convention Center (OSCO) in Cheongju. Held annually since 2019 as a public-private-industry-academia forum. Free entry, 10:00–17:00 (to 15:00 Friday). A policy-and-industry event rather than a festival.

title: Gimje Horizon Festival
overview: The Gimje Horizon Festival is Korea’s only Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival dedicated to traditional farming culture, as designated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. Centered around Byeokgolje Reservoir, Korea’s oldest and largest irrigation facility, the festival celebrates the nation's rich farming heritage. Set against the region's expansive horizon, the festival features the Presidential Cup National Nongak Competition, along with hands-on agricultural experiences such as cooking rice over a traditional wood-fired stove, catching grasshoppers, and harvesting rice. Visitors can also take part in traditional events, including the Byeokgolje Twin Dragon Play, inspired by a local legend, and the Ipseok Tug-of-War for a bountiful harvest.

title: Jeongseon Arirang Festival
overview: The Jeongseon Arirang Festival is Jeongseon County’s signature cultural tourism festival created to preserve and carry forward the history, cultural value, and traditions of Jeongseon Arirang, one of Korea’s best-known folk songs. Celebrating Arirang, which is inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, the festival brings together performances that blend tradition with contemporary elements, parades, hands-on programs, exhibitions, and various cultural and artistic events for visitors of all ages. The festival is also shaped by the local community, with residents taking on an active role in its planning and operation. Programs connecting Jeongseon’s cultural and tourism resources help boost the local economy and attract more visitors to the region. Building on the cultural legacy of Arirang and the unique traditions of Jeongseon, the festival seeks to establish itself as Korea’s leading Arirang celebration and grow into a global cultural tourism festival that people around the world can enjoy and relate to.

title: Gyeryong Military Culture Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The 2025 Gyeryong Military Culture Festival will take place from September 17 (Wed.) to 21 (Sun.) at the Gyeryongdae Runway and venues across the city under the slogan “Gyeryong’s Dream, K-Military Culture Taking Flight to the World!” Recognized as one of Korea’s leading festivals, the event will offer a wide range of performances and activities for visitors of all ages. Highlights include the opening celebration, Military Culture Festa concerts featuring rock, trot, K-pop, and other genres, guest performances by military bands and honor guards, and road parade. Visitors can also enjoy hands-on activities and special programs including Extreme Special Experiences, all designed to raise the profile of military culture. This year’s festival will also feature a special Wellness Life Exhibition that brings together military culture and lifestyle in a new festival experience.
place: Gyeryongdae Runway and various locations across Gyeryong-si

title: Busan International Performing Arts Market (BPAM)
overview: A festival-style performing-arts market in Busan, now in its fourth year: artists, producers, and presenters from Korea and abroad showcase productions, build networks, and negotiate distribution — but unlike a pure trade fair, the showcases are open for ordinary audiences to enjoy. Venues center on Dongseo University's Centum campus and the Haeundae Culture Center. Fees vary by program; 10:00–22:00.

title: Ground Forces Festival
overview: Korea's largest military culture festival, hosted by the ROK Army on the runway of Gyeryongdae — the tri-service headquarters. Five days of the latest Korean and US combat equipment on display (much of it climbable), Army TIGER and drone-bot demonstrations, AI-based combat systems at the army policy hall, and a full slate of military pageantry: military band and honor guard shows, taekwondo demonstrations, military police motorcycle drills, and road parades. Free, 09:00–17:00 over the Chuseok holiday window.

title: Cheonan World Dance Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Cheonan World Dance Festival is a global event that brings everyone together through dance, transcending nationalities and language barriers. Dancers from all over the world gather in Cheonan to participate in various festival programs. The National Dance Competition is the highlight of the festival, with a total prize of about 100 million won. There is also the Street Dance Parade across the city center and the International Dance Competition in which dance teams from across the globe participate. Other shows include the energetic performances of the National University Cheerleading Competition and the exciting “Improv Dance Battle,” where everyone can join in on the fun.
