title: Sancheong Medicinal Herb Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Sancheong Herbal Medicinal Festival is a celebration for those interested in traditional herbal medicine. Donguibogam (Principles and Practice of Eastern Medicine) and its author, Heo Jun, are highly regarded in Korean medicine. Sancheong, where Heo Jun studied, is home to Jirisan Mountain, which is often seen as a treasure trove by Korean medicine doctors due to being a habitat of over 1,000 species of medicinal herbs. The festival features Korean medicine clinics offering treatments like acupuncture, while the festival square is transformed into an herbal garden with photo zones, tea drinking spots, spaces for making herbal flower pots, and exhibitions and sales of herbal flower pot goods. Visitors can also participate in making herbal sweet rice puffs, nostalgic herbal dalgona candy, herbal cocktails, and herbal tea brewed in a large decoction pot.◎ Dongui bogamDongui bogam is a medical encyclopedia completed in 1610, written by Heo Jun after a meticulous study and observation of medical books and practices of China and Joseon. It is considered the best medical encyclopedia in the East and was registered as a UNESCO Memory of the World in 2009.

title: Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival
titleFull: Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival (포항 해뜨면 국수축제)
overview: The  Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival is a grand culinary festival held at Ara Plaza in Guryongpo on the Homi Peninsula. The festival’s name intuitively captures the symbolic significance of the Homi Peninsula—where the sun rises first in South Korea. Visitors can sample everything from Pohang’s best noodle restaurants to representative noodles from across the country, global noodles, and recipes by star chefs—all in one place. The festival also offers plenty of entertainment for all ages, including a music festival, cooking competitions, and retro experiences. Equipped with an eco-friendly system featuring smart QR ordering and reusable containers, the festival offers a unique culinary journey exclusive to Pohang—where the flavors and excitement are first awakened amidst the vibrant energy of the East Sea.
place: The area around Guryongpo Ara Plaza

title: Bupyeong Pungmul Festival
overview: Celebrating its 30th edition, the Bupyeong Pungmul Festival brings rhythm, excitement, and community spirit to the heart of the city. Since its launch in 1997, the festival has grown into one of Korea’s leading traditional cultural and performing arts festivals. For nearly three decades, it has filled the urban landscape with the vibrant sounds of Korean pungmul, creating a dynamic space where citizens and artists come together. At the heart of the festival are the pungmul troupes from Bupyeong’s 22 neighborhoods, whose lively rhythms have long served as a powerful force for community unity. Held for three days from October 2 to 4, 2026, the 30th Bupyeong Pungmul Festival carries special significance as it reflects on the traditions built over the past three decades while celebrating a new chapter for the future. This year’s edition will be bigger and more colorful than ever, expanding into the Gulpocheon Stream area, an iconic symbol of Bupyeong’s urban regeneration, and presenting an even wider variety of programs and experiences.

title: Busan International Rock Festival
overview: First held in 2000, the Busan International Rock Festival is Korea’s first and longest-running international rock festival. In 2026, the 27th edition will take place over three days, from Friday, October 2 to Sunday, October 4, at Samnak Eco Park, featuring a diverse lineup of Korean and international artists. Stages set throughout the park will showcase everything from emerging talent to world-renowned headliners. Beyond the performances, visitors can also enjoy a variety of festival attractions, including interactive games, food court lounges, camping zones, and other special side events.

title: Anheung Steamed Bun Festival
overview: Anheung's jjinppang — soft steamed buns with red-bean filling — made this Hoengseong village famous, and its 18th festival celebrates them with a full weekend: the bun-and-dokkaebi (goblin) themed main festival drawing on local folklore, the retro 'Saturday Saturday is a Singer' 90s-music stage, roaming goblin performance squads, bun-themed events, and a closing residents' singing contest. Free, 10:00–20:00, in the aptly named 'steaming bun village'. Come hungry.

title: Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival
titleFull: Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival (안성맞춤 남사당 바우덕이축제)
overview: The Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival is centered on Namsadang Nori, which is inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It preserves and builds on the artistic legacy of Baudeogi, the first female kkokdusoe (troupe leader) of the Joseon era, and the vibrant traditions of Anseong’s Namsadang troupe. The festival offers a rich mix of programs for all ages, from traditional cultural experiences and performances by Korean and international artists to folk performances from around the world. Visitors can also explore the Anseong Old Market, which recreates the lively atmosphere of one of the three major marketplaces in Korea during the Joseon period. Highlights include jultagi (tightrope walking) and Namsadang Nori, giving visitors a close-up look at some of Korea’s most dynamic traditional performing arts. Performances that blend traditional and contemporary elements make the festival an engaging way to experience the energy and appeal of Korean culture. Bringing together history, culture, performance, and tourism, the Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival has established itself as a cultural tourism festival enjoyed by visitors from Korea and abroad, and continues to grow as one of Korea’s leading festivals celebrating traditional culture.
place: Anseong Matchum Land & Anseongcheon Stream area

title: Soraepogu Festival
overview: Soraepogu Festival, a maritime ecology festival, has been held annually since 2001. Sorae Port has become a popular attraction, visited by over 7 million domestic and international tourists each year. During the festival, visitors can enjoy Sorae Marsh Eco Park, Shrimp Tower, and Haeoreumhosu Lake. Festival programs include seafood-catching events like shrimp and crab catching, various cultural performances, and engaging events.
fee: Free (separate charge may apply to activities)

title: Cheongwon Life Festival
overview: Cheongju's eco-agriculture festival, running since 2008 around the Cheongwon Life brand of premium local produce. The rural theme park in Ochang fills with themed exhibitions, hands-on farm programs, cultural performances, and a direct farmers' market connecting growers and consumers — with a strong education angle for children on where food comes from. Entry 5,000 won; children, teens, pregnant women, and seniors free. 10:00–20:00.
fee: 5,000 won (children, youth, pregnant women, seniors free)

title: Goseong Pollack Festival
overview: Goseong on Gangwon's north coast was Korea's pollack capital, and this festival reworks that heritage on the beach at Geojin: a pollack gourmet zone with live chef cooking and cook-it-yourself sessions, fish crafts and games, bare-hand fish catching, a beach playground, and a silent-DJ party on the sand. Residents, soldiers, and students run much of the program themselves. Distributed stages and shuttles keep the beachfront lively all day. Free entry, 11:00–19:00.

title: Yeoncheon Goryeo Ginseng Festival
overview: Yeoncheon sits on the 38th parallel with the latitude, climate, and soil rated ideal for six-year ginseng — the gold standard of Korean insam. Its festival, in the plaza by Yeoncheon Station, showcases the county's Gaeseong-lineage Goryeo ginseng with exhibitions, direct farm sales, tastings, and hands-on programs, putting growers and buyers face to face. Free, 10:00–17:00. Good for stocking up at source prices on Korea's most famous health root.

title: Wanju Wild & Local Food Festival
overview: Wanju — the county that pioneered Korea's local-food movement — throws its flagship festival in the Gosan recreational forest under the 2026 slogan 'burning wild'. Fire is the theme: open-fire oven roasting, local bushcraft, potato pit-steaming, and large fire events, alongside stream water play, straw-bale slides, a 'local table' cooked by the women's associations of all 13 townships, a farm-produce market, and a wild EDM party after dark. Free, 10:00–22:00.

title: Geumsan World K-Insam Festival
overview: Held in Geumsan, Chungcheongnam-do, long known as the home of ginseng with a history spanning more than 1,500 years, the Geumsan World K-Insam Festival invites visitors of all ages to experience ginseng in every form. The festival features hands-on programs such as ginseng digging, red ginseng facial mask treatments, red ginseng foot baths, traditional ginseng culture experiences, and the International Ginseng Trade Fair, along with opportunities to shop for ginseng products at reasonable prices. Across the festival grounds, visitors can also enjoy healthy dishes made with ginseng and medicinal herbs. Held annually since 1981, the festival has become one of Korea’s leading industry-based festivals. It has been named one of Korea’s Top Cultural Tourism Festivals by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism 10 times and was selected as an Asian Specialty Festival by IFEA World in 2024. Today, the Geumsan World K-Insam Festival continues to grow as a global festival enjoyed by visitors from Korea and beyond.

title: Uiryeong Rich Rich Festival
overview: In the middle of the Nam River at Uiryeong stands Solbawi, the 'cauldron rock', with a legend: great fortunes will be born within 20 ri of it. The founders of Samsung, LG, and Hyosung were all born nearby — and the county has run with it. The fifth Rich Rich Festival invites visitors to soak up the rock's money-luck through wealth-themed experiences, performances, and family programs around town. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–22:00. Unapologetically fun feng-shui tourism.

title: Anadream Safety Festival
overview: Gyeongbuk's largest safety-experience event, held since 2021 in the 'thousand-year forest' by the provincial office in Andong. Some 40 agencies run 70-plus hands-on safety programs — fire-engine and rescue-equipment displays, rescue-dog training demos, drone demonstrations, a firefighting parade, and a kids' safety school — leavened with magic and bubble shows, stamp tours, and treasure hunts. Free, 10:00–17:00, and genuinely useful for families with children.

title: Gunsan Time Travel Festival
overview: Gunsan preserves one of Korea's densest concentrations of Japanese colonial-era architecture, and its signature festival turns that district into a stage for time travel. Large flash-mob performances recreate the era's global currents, the 'March 5th' event fills the streets with the cry of the 1919 independence movement, and a time-currency system converts participation into souvenirs and discounts. Retro 7080 games and food round out a festival that manages to be both a history lesson and a proper day out. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–21:00.
place: Old city hall plaza and Time Travel Village

title: Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival is an event that continues the practice of making wishes by floating colorful lanterns down the Namgang River. This practice of over 400 years originated from the Siege of Jinju in 1592. The festival begins at sunset when lanterns of various shapes and sizes are lit on the Namgang River. World Pungmul lanterns, wish lanterns, traditional lanterns, religious lanterns, and customized lanterns embroider the night with colorful lights. Fireworks and lighting shows are held against the backdrop of this beautiful night view, along with various cultural shows. The festival operates food trucks where visitors can enjoy delicious foods from around the world. ◎ The Siege of Jinju and YudeungDuring the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592, yudeung (oil lanterns) were lit in the battle at Jinjuseong Fortress to stop the Japanese army from crossing the Namgang River. The lanterns were also used as a means of contacting families outside the fortress.
place: Areas of Jinjuseong Fortress and Namgang River

title: Gangnam Festival
overview: Gangnam Festival, the largest urban festival unfolding across the entire city center, begins with a spectacular street parade to mark the opening. The festival transforms the entirety of Gangnam into one massive festival space featuring K-POP concerts, family concerts for the whole family to enjoy, a Fashion & Beauty Festa combining K-fashion and performance, and a Beer & Food Festa offering diverse culinary experiences. As a global K-Culture festival combining the city's energy with Hallyu content, the Gangnam Festival is a representative cultural tourism event that promotes the charms of Gangnam to the world.
place: Areas of Dosandaero Avenue, Gaepo-dong Maru Park, and Bongeunsa Temple

title: King Jeongjo Filial Piety Festival
overview: Hwaseong's flagship history festival at Jeongjo Hyo Park, honoring the king whose devotion to his father shaped the region. The centerpiece reenacts the relocation of Crown Prince Sado's tomb to Yungneung — considered Joseon's finest burial site — and on October 4 the great royal procession of 1795 sets out from Dongtan Central Park in full period costume, one of Korea's grandest parade reenactments. Traditional performances and family programs fill the park throughout. Free, 10:00–18:00.

title: Yeongju Punggi Ginseng Festival
overview: Punggi is one of Korea's most storied ginseng regions, and its festival lands in October when the root's nutrients peak. The program leans into health: ginseng-cuisine tastings, ginseng-peeling contests, and wellness exhibitions, plus ritual reenactments — the founding-site rite, Governor Ju Se-bung's procession (the 16th-century official credited with starting cultivation here), and the great ginseng ceremony. Fresh roots, red ginseng, and processed goods sell at grower prices. Free entry, 10:00–20:00.
place: Namwoncheon stream and Punggi Ginseng Park

title: Yeongju Museom Single-Log Bridge Festival
overview: Museom is a riverside heritage village wrapped in a bend of the Naeseongcheon stream, reached for centuries by a narrow single-log bridge over the water and white sand. The festival reenacts the village's life rites — a traditional wedding procession arriving by palanquin, a funeral bier procession departing — alongside bridge-crossing performances, barefoot sand walking, parade games, rope experiences, a poetry contest, a national photo contest, and a stamp tour. Free, 10:00–18:00. One of the most photogenic festivals in the country.

title: Dongdaemun Festival
overview: For one day, 700 meters of Janghan-ro go car-free under the theme 'a new gallop of culture' — a nod to the street's history, from the Joseon military horse pastures of Janghanpyeong to the modern used-car district. Performances, hands-on programs, and citizen events run the length of the road, including a pop-up roller rink and 'my car becomes a shop', where residents' own vehicles turn into market stalls. Free, 11:00–22:00.
place: Janghan-ro (700m, Woori Bank crossing to Jangan crossing)

title: Baekje Cultural Festival
overview: Baekje Cultural Festival first started in 1955 and aims to bring the history and culture of the Baekje era to life, taking place at UNESCO-recognized sites throughout Gongju and Buyeo. The festival operates as an open event where the history and culture of Baekje, local businesses, and the daily lives of residents harmonize, and is expected to provide visitors with a special cultural experience where the past and present coexist.
place: Buyeo historic sites (Jeongnimsaji Temple Site, Seoktap-ro, Gwanbuk-ri)

title: Yeongju Punggi Insam Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Ginseng is a well-known traditional Korean medicinal herb. High quality ginseng in Korea is mostly produced in Punggi, a region in Yeongju, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and the place where the Punggi Ginseng Festival takes place. The festival features health-related exhibits and offers opportunities to taste healthy ginseng dishes at the ginseng cooking exhibition. Visitors can also participate in Punggi ginseng-related interesting activities such as making Punggi ginseng wine and peeling ginseng in the traditional Korean way. The festival offers a variety of ginseng products, including fresh ginseng, original ginseng, red ginseng, and ginseng processed foods, which are all grown by local farmers in Yeongju and sold at reasonable prices. Additionally, the festival showcases local specialties and symbols such as ginseng and Yeongju apples through oil lantern displays along Namwoncheon Stream. With so many attractions, visitors are sure to have a great time at the festival.
sponsor: Yeongju  Punggi Insam Festival Organizing Committee

title: Chuncheon Ani-Toy Festival
overview: A three-day subculture fair at the Animation Museum in Chuncheon, gathering animation, characters, art toys, figures, goods, and creator content in one place. Brand and artist booths, industry experience programs, and sales floors run side by side, bringing companies, creators, fans, and collectors together — with plenty for families in between the collector stalls. Free, 11:00–17:00 over the early-October holiday weekend.

title: Suwon Hwaseong Festival
overview: The Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival reimagines, through a contemporary lens, the most magnificent moments of King Jeongjo’s eight-day royal procession to Hwaseong in 1795. Historic scenes recorded in the Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe come vividly to life through high-quality cultural programs. Visitors can also take part in the King Jeongjo Royal Parade, the largest royal procession reenactment in Korea, where citizens and guests from around the world become part of the spectacle. As a leading global festival, the Suwon Hwaseong Festival offers a unique opportunity to experience the joy of a celebration that transcends time and space while bringing people together in the historic setting of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress.
sponsor: Suwon-si, Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival Organizing Committee, Suwon Cultural Foundation

title: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade
titleFull: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade (정조대왕 능행차 공동재현)
overview: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade to Hwaseong Fortress recreates one of the most remarkable events of the Joseon dynasty. In 1795, King Jeongjo traveled from Seoul to Suwon to celebrate the 60th birthday of his mother, Queen Heonui, sharing the eight-day journey with the people along the route. Based on records from the "Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe," the festival faithfully reenacts the royal procession with traditional costumes, performances, and ceremonial displays. Held through the cooperation of Seoul, Gyeonggi-do, Suwon, and Hwaseong, the event offers visitors a chance to experience the grandeur and spirit of a historic royal celebration.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government, Gyeonggi Province, Suwon Special City, Hwaseong Special City

title: Gumcheon Siheung Haenggung Cultural Festival
overview: The 'Geumcheon Siheung Palace Cultural Festival' is a representative historical and cultural festival of Geumcheon-gu that embodies the district's historical identity and cultural artistic significance. The festival offers diverse programs for all residents to enjoy together.

title: Creative X Seongsu
overview: A culture-and-creative-industry festival spread across Seongsu-dong — Seoul's converted-factory district often compared to Brooklyn. Anchored at the S-Factory, the program mixes themed exhibitions by culture-tech companies, conferences and pitches, 'Play Seongsu' turning the whole district into a game theme park, gallery exhibitions, a craft flea market, an outdoor fashion show, and an urban music festival. Fees and hours vary by program — check before you go, then let the neighborhood's cafes fill the gaps.

title: Hamyang Wild Ginseng Festival
overview: Hamyang's mountain-grown ginseng — raised above 500m in germanium-rich soil, dense-fleshed and high in saponin — is billed as Korea's premium sansam, backed by the country's first wild-ginseng traceability system. The festival unfolds in Sangnim Park, a 1,100-year-old planted forest and Natural Monument, with programs reviving the culture of the simmani (wild-ginseng hunters), local-produce markets, and forest-and-culture events. Free, 10:00–21:00; the ancient forest alone justifies the visit.

title: Naju Yeongsangang River Festival
overview: Naju's five-day autumn festival in the Yeongsangang Garden, where the wide river meets landscaped grounds. Days bring garden strolls, family programs, and Naju food (the city is famous for its beef-broth gukbap and pears); nights turn to illuminated riverscapes and headline performances. A stay-all-day festival that doubles as an introduction to one of Jeolla's oldest river towns. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection
titleFull: Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection (광주 추억의 충장축제)
addr: 226-22, Geumnam-ro, Dong-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection is Gwangju’s largest signature festival, originating on Chungjang-ro in Dong-gu. Built around the universal theme of memories, it is Korea’s first festival of its kind, bringing together people of all generations and backgrounds. Geumnam-ro and May 18 Democracy Square, the festival’s main venues, hold profound significance in the history of democracy. They symbolize not only remembrance of the past but also Gwangju’s journey toward a hopeful future. Recognized for its excellence, the festival has been designated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as both a Cultural Tourism Festival and an Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival. It has also gained international recognition through consecutive honors at the Asia’s Pinnacle Awards and Gwangju’s designation as a World Festival City. Looking ahead, the festival aims to grow into a truly international event through collaboration with the Asia Culture Center, embracing the cultures and shared memories of Asia. In doing so, it strengthens Gwangju's role as a leading cultural city of Asia and provides a meaningful platform for communication and harmony through culture.
place: Geumnam-ro, Chungjang-ro, May 18 Democracy Square, and Art Street
sponsor: Gwangju Dong-gu, Dong-gu Culture & Tourism Foundation, Chungjang Festival Organizing Committee

title: Gwangju Busking World Cup
overview: An international street-music competition staged across downtown Gwangju, centered on the May 18 Democracy Plaza. Buskers from Korea and abroad — vocalists, bands, acoustic acts, performers — battle through preliminaries and finals judged by a professional panel, turning the city's streets into open stages for days. Free, 13:00–22:00; the finals nights draw the biggest crowds.

title: Hoengseong Hanu Festival
overview: Hoengseong Hanu Festival is the biggest hanu (Korean cattle) festival in Korea. Visitors can buy hanu and local agricultural products at a discounted price. The festival consists of various programs across three themes: food, culture and arts, and experiences.
fee: Free (separate charge may apply to activities)

title: Jeongeup Gujeolcho Flower Festival
overview: Every October, 150,000 square meters of white gujeolcho (Korean chrysanthemum) bloom beneath a pine forest along a clear mountain stream in Jeongeup — the largest such garden in the East, and one of Korea's most beloved photography spots, whether in dawn mist or afternoon light. Walking paths thread the pine-scented flower hills, joined by local-heritage experience programs and farm-produce markets. Ticketed entry, 08:30–17:30.

title: Jeungpyeong Insamgol Festival
overview: Jeungpyeong grows about two-thirds of Chungbuk's ginseng, and its harvest festival has grown into a full-spectrum event: the 'In-Maek Party' pairing ginseng with beer and EDM, an international youth festival, a national song contest, a national busking festival, and nightly fireworks. Family and health experience zones, on-site produce auctions, and traditional ssireum wrestling round it out. Free, 10:00–20:00 along the Bogangcheon sports park.

title: Imsil N Cheese Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Imsil N Cheese Festival is held every fall in Imsil, the birthplace of cheese production in Korea, at Imsil Cheese Theme Park and Imsil Cheese Village, which are proud symbols of the region. Visitors are greeted by the aroma of delicious cheese as they wander through the beautiful chrysanthemum flower garden with millions of blooms. The festival features more than 10 main themes and 70 programs centered around cheese, offering a rich and diverse experience. Events include Imsil N Busking, kids’ concerts, various craft experiences, and a stamp rally tour, ensuring plenty of fun for everyone.◎ TipIt is recommended to bring a tripod or an extra battery pack to take many pictures of the quaint buildings and flower gardens at the festival.
place: Imsil Cheese Theme Park, Imsil Cheese Village, and the Imsil-eup area

title: Jangseong Hwangryonggang Autumn Flower Festival
titleFull: Jangseong Hwangryonggang Autumn Flower Festival (장성 황룡강 가을꽃축제)
overview: The Jangseong Hwangryonggang River Autumn Flower Festival is set against the backdrop of the 3.2-kilometer-long Hwangryonggang River. The festival features gardens where visitors can admire a variety of autumn flowers, such as cosmos and zinnias. This festival allows visitors to observe the changing seasons up close as they stroll through the gardens along the riverside and admire the flowers within them. It also features hands-on activities for visitors to participate in, as well as performances by local artists and invited singers, making it a festival that welcomes people of all ages. With rest areas and amenities provided throughout the festival grounds, along with displays of local agricultural specialties and food, this festival allows visitors to experience all that Jangseong has to offer in one place.

title: Silla Culture Festival
overview: Gyeongju's flagship festival since 1962, now in its 53rd edition, staged among the city's actual Silla monuments. The Hwabaek ceremony reenacts royal history against Woljeonggyo Bridge; a street-arts festival and Silk Road Festa fill the historic quarter; and the Hwarang Hip-hop Festa puts Korea's top hip-hop acts on stage in front of ancient burial mounds — a collision of eras you will only see here. The Moonlight Market adds local food into the night. Free, 15:00–24:00.

title: Welcome to Singwan-dong
overview: A youth street festival on the university strip of Singwan-dong in Gongju, run since 2022 as part of the city's culture-city initiative. Busking competitions, street performances, a beer festa, flea markets, and hands-on programs line the college road, with students, residents, and merchants co-running the show. Timed alongside the Baekje Culture Festival, so you can pair ancient-kingdom pageantry with a student-quarter night out. Free, 14:00–21:00.
sponsor: Gongju City · Gongju Culture & Tourism Foundation

title: Incheon Open Port Heritage Night Tour
overview: The 11th night festival in Incheon's open-port quarter — the district of 1880s customs houses, banks, and warehouses where modern Korea first met the world. The classic '8 nights' program (night views, night roads, night history, night food, night market and more) threads performances, exhibitions, and food through three evenings of specially opened heritage buildings, with lodging promotions for those who stay. Free, 18:00–22:00; Chinatown and Songwol-dong's fairytale village are next door.

title: Seosan Haemi Eupseong Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Seosan Haemi Eupseong Festival is a cultural festival held at Seosan Haemieupseong Walled Town, an ancient fortress with a 600-year history. The festival combines light, music, and the historic fortress to create a fantastic nighttime scenery and offers content for all generations. During the day, visitors can enjoy sophisticated performances while picnicking, and at night, they can partake in a vibrant evening stroll.

title: Daejeon Donggu-dongnak Festival
overview: A festival behind Daejeon Station, spreading through the east plaza and along the Daedongcheon stream — the gateway to Soje-dong's retro cafe alley and the old railway officials' village. World-food theme booths, all-ages game zones, a streamside 'booknic' of books and rest, a bakery competition (this is the city of bakeries), and chef cooking shows give it an urban, food-forward flavor distinct from Korea's rural festivals. Free, 11:00–22:00.
place: Soje-dong east plaza and Daedongcheon stream

title: Saenggeo Jincheon Culture Festival
overview: Jincheon's folk festival, running since 1979 on the Baekgokcheon riverside — the county's biggest annual event, drawing tens of thousands. The name comes from the old saying 'saenggeo Jincheon': the best place to live. Folk-arts competitions, a local-food cook-off, ssireum wrestling, performances, exhibitions, hands-on programs, and a food market fill the grounds, with the county's famously abundant farm produce on sale throughout. Free, 09:00–22:00 (varies by day).

title: Siheung Wolgot Port Festival
overview: A harbor festival at Wolgot, the fishing port folded into the city on Gyeonggi's west coast. The draws are hands-on: fishing-boat rides, bare-hand fish catching, and king-prawn catching, plus surprise seafood auctions, a dried-seafood wholesale market, and salted-shrimp making. Evenings bring the Moonlight Concert and opening and closing fireworks over the water. Free, 10:00–22:00 — Seoul's nearest taste of working-port festival culture.

title: GHOST Festival
titleFull: GHOST Festival (Gyeonggi Hallyu OST Festival) (GHOST(경기 한류 OST) 페스티벌)
overview:
The Gyeonggi Hallyu OST Music Festival, or the GHOST Festival, is Korea’s first festival dedicated to original soundtracks. It brings together the memorable music of K-dramas, films, and animation alongside performances by renowned K-pop artists. The festival unfolds across a series of themed programs including romance, science fiction, and fantasy. Each day presents a rich spectrum of performances, from lyrical ballads and dynamic band music to grand orchestral compositions. Accompanied by large-scale media art and immersive stage production, the festival offers visitors a cinematic experience, allowing them to feel as though they have stepped into the world of a film.

In addition to the performances, visitors can enjoy a wide range of activities such as K-content experiences, Hallyu cultural programs, diverse culinary offerings, and camping facilities. These elements come together to create a vibrant cultural destination where visitors of all ages, including families, friends, and couples, can spend a full day enjoying the festival.

title: Hwasun Jeokbyeok Culture Festival
overview: Hwasun Jeokbyeok — the 'Red Cliffs' rising over a reservoir in a restricted watershed — is one of Jeolla's most striking and least-accessible landscapes, and this festival is the easiest way in. Programs include guided cliff walks, the GEO environmental concert, wellness sessions under the cliffs, local-produce markets, and community programs, with free shuttle buses running to the site. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–17:00.
place: Iseo Community Center and Hwasun Jeokbyeok cliffs

title: 8th Yecheon International Smartphone Film Festival
overview: A film festival for movies shot entirely on smartphones — the device 'everyone' carries — running in Yecheon since 2019 and now Korea's flagship smartphone-film event. Entries from an open international call are judged and screened, with the awards ceremony and a community film-festival day on October 9. Free, 11:00–20:20, in a green county better known for archery and old pavilions.

title: Sejong Hangeul Festival
overview: The Sejong Hangeul Festival is the only festival in Korea dedicated to Hangeul, the Korean alphabet. Held every year around Hangeul Day, it is Sejong City’s signature celebration of the Korean writing system. Launched in 2013, the festival honors the vision behind King Sejong’s creation of Hangeul. In 2025, it was renamed the Sejong Hangeul Festival from its former name, the Sejong Festival. The festival brings the beauty and creativity of Hangeul to life through performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs with a fresh, contemporary touch. Open to visitors of all ages and nationalities, it offers an easy and engaging way to experience the appeal of Hangeul and the spirit of King Sejong in the heart of the city. Blending traditional and contemporary arts and culture, the festival continues to grow as a distinctive cultural tourism event unique to Sejong City.
place: Sejong Lake Park, Sejong Central Park

title: Chuncheon Makguksu & Dakgalbi Festival
overview: Chuncheon Makguksu & Dakgalbi Festival celebrates dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and makguksu (buckwheat noodles), two of the most famous specialties of the city of Chuncheon. During this festival, the area is full of booths selling buckwheat noodles and spicy stir-fried chicken. The festival offers plenty of ways to experience these two local foods.
place: Streamside between Hyojagyo Bridge and Gongjigyo Bridge
sponsor: Chuncheon Makguksu & Dakgalbi Festival Organizing Committee

title: Seoul Design Week 2026
overview: Seoul's design festival, in its 13th year, runs 12 days under the theme 'The Design Recipe'. The DDP Design Fair stages a 'market of tastes' where visitors assemble Seoul-found brands around their own preferences, while exhibitions span DDP, Seongsu, and Hongdae: works by 100 working Seoul designers, international studio process shows, and goods pop-ups full of 'next Seoul'. Early bird 9,000 won, regular 15,000 won; 10:00–20:00.
place: Dongdaemun Design Plaza and venues in Seongsu and Hongdae

title: Yeongdong Nangye Korean Traditional Music Festival
titleFull: Yeongdong Nangye Korean Traditional Music Festival (영동난계국악축제)
overview: The Yeongdong Nangye Korean Traditional Music Festival is an annual performing arts festival dedicated to gugak, Korea’s traditional music and one of Yeongdong-gun’s most treasured cultural assets. The festival also honors the musical legacy of Nangye Park Yeon, one of Korea’s most renowned traditional musicians, while contributing to the preservation and promotion of traditional performing arts. Building on the achievements of the 2025 Yeongdong World Traditional Music & Arts Expo, the 57th festival seeks to introduce gugak, a treasured element of Korea's cultural heritage, to a wider global audience and contribute to a new wave of global interest in Korean culture. As Korea’s only festival dedicated to traditional Korean music, it offers a wide range of performances and hands-on programs that reinterpret traditional performing arts for contemporary audiences. Through programs that reflect the unique character of Yeongdong, the festival also helps transform local cultural resources into a tourism assets. At the same time, it encourages community participation, enhances cultural engagement among residents, and serves as a vibrant celebration of local unity.
sponsor: Yeongdong Festival Tourism Foundation, Nangye Commemorative Conference

title: Sunchang Jangryu Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Experience the most iconic spicy flavor of Korean cuisine, gochujang (red chili paste). This festival takes place in Sunchang, the renowned home of gochujang. Visitors can try spicy and savory dishes made with Sunchang gochujang, partake in programs such as making red chili paste, and check out the festival’s performances, exhibitions, and shops. The biggest attraction is the “Sunchang gochujang offering procession to the King.” It is an reenactment based on the records of King Taejo's (born Yi Seong-gye), founder of the Joseon dynasty, love for the taste of Sunchang gochujang. During the event, a music procession and porters with a wagon loaded with crocks of chili paste perform a march around the village. Visitors can also check out the new Fermentation Theme Park, where they can learn the scientific principles of food through microbial experiments.◎ TipTteokbokki is a must-eat Korean street food. Don’t miss the “Sunchang Tteokbokki Town,” where you can try a variety of tteokbokki dishes made using Sunchang’s fermented sauces.
place: Area of Sunchang Gochujang Village and Fermentation Theme Park
fee: Free (fees may apply to programs)  * Discount may apply to guests in red clothing

title: Chungbuk Garden Expo in Yeongdong
overview: The second Chungcheongbuk-do garden expo lands in Yeongdong — the county of gugak (traditional music) and fruit — for four days at Yongdu Park. Garden-industry exhibitions, experience and flea-market zones, and garden-culture performances share the grounds with citizen-made gardens selected by open call, all threaded with live gugak. It deliberately overlaps the Nangye Gugak Festival, so traditional music carries across both events. Free, 09:00–18:00.

title: Gochang Moyang Fortress Festival
overview: Gochang Eupseong (Moyang Fortress) is Korea's best-preserved town wall, and its festival is built on a charming legend: circle the wall once to cure leg ailments, twice for long life, three times for paradise. The signature dapseong wall-walk becomes a nighttime moonlight round combined with the ganggangsullae circle dance, joined by a 1,000-resident street parade, the 'Returns 1453' time-travel program inside the fortress, and markets of Gochang specialties. Free, 10:00–22:00.

title: Hurshimchung Bräu Oktoberfest
overview: Hurshimchung Bräu Oktoberfest takes place in October at the outdoor space of Hotel Nongshim in Busan. The festival aims to create a fun experience for visitors of all ages, despite the main theme of the festival being beer. Enjoy special brews made by the brewmasters of Hurshimchung, as well as the tasty foods prepared by the chefs of Hotel Nongshim while watching a range of performances.
place: Outdoor space & beer garden of Hotel Nongshim

title: Chilgok Nakdonggang Peace Festival
overview: Chilgok was the last line of defense in the 1950 Battle of the Nakdong River, and this festival — the 13th — honors that history under the slogan 'a boy becomes a boy soldier', spotlighting the young student-soldiers often left out of the heroic narrative. Peace-themed performances, participatory programs, and food zones fill the Chilgokbo eco-park, co-organized with the Second Operations Command. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–22:00.
sponsor: Chilgok Culture & Tourism Foundation · ROK Second Operations Command

title: 30th Ulsan Whale Festival
overview: Jangsaengpo was once Korea's whaling capital; today its Whale Culture Special Zone celebrates coexistence instead, and the festival turns 30 with the theme 'The whale's invitation — a 30th birthday party!'. Four days bring a whale parade, themed performances, a 300-citizen chorus, special fireworks, kids' festa, AR and AI whale experiences, an anniversary archive exhibition, and food zones — plus year-round attractions like the whale-watching cruise and ecology hall. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Ho-Camp Returns
overview: A family camping festival in its ninth year, organized by the camping YouTube channels Ho-Camp, GogoTwoMing, and Hong-Camp at the Neowaduri farm campground in Okcheon. The weekend runs a welcome party, singing contest, laser-tag survival games, a second-hand camping-gear auction, a kids' cinema, party night, and prize giveaways. Participation is per family (from 180,000 won for two adults and two children) — book ahead; it is a committed camping crowd.
fee: From 180,000 won per family (2 adults + 2 children)

title: Mokpo Port Festival
addr: 6 Samhak-ro 92beon-gil, Mokpo-si, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*“Mokpo is a port.” This phrase is familiar to Koreans as both a movie title and a popular song. Mokpo, one of three major ports in Korea, is a key center for trade and logistics. The Mokpo Port Festival recreates the traditional Pasi Market culture of Mokpo Port, offering a variety of food, entertainment, and experiences. Visitors can participate in live auctions at a ship for fresh seafood and enjoy the ocean view while grilling their purchases at the cooking station. In addition, the festival features a variety of maritime parades, navy band performances, and shows by art troupes from Mokpo’s overseas sister cities, all reflecting Mokpo’s identity as a port city.◎ Pasi MarketA market formed on the sea where merchant ships and traders gather near fishing grounds.
place: Areas of Mokpo Port & Samhakdo Island

title: Geumjeongsanseong Fortress Festival
overview: Geumjeongsanseong is Korea's largest mountain fortress, ringing the peaks above Busan — and with Geumjeongsan newly designated a national park in 2026, this year's festival celebrates both. Three days of history, culture, and arts programs at the fortress plaza commemorate the wall's construction, blending the mountain's ecology with its military heritage. Running since 1996. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–19:00; combine with the fortress-village makgeolli, a Busan institution.

title: Gimhae Heritage Night Tour
overview: A night festival among the monuments of Gaya — the ancient kingdom whose royal tomb of King Suro, Daeseong-dong tumuli, and Sureungwon garden anchor central Gimhae. The '8 nights' program lights the heritage quarter with night views, story walks, performances, exhibitions, food, and markets, letting visitors meet Korea's 'fourth kingdom' — the one that never made the standard Three Kingdoms narrative — on atmospheric terms. Free, 16:00–23:00.
place: King Suro's Tomb and Sureungwon area
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Gyeongsangnam-do · Gimhae City

title: 14th Gyeonggi Garden Culture Expo
overview: A garden expo at Dumulmeori — the celebrated confluence where the North and South Han Rivers meet — and Semiwon, the province's first designated local garden, famous for its lotus ponds. The 2026 theme, 'Dumulmeori: four colors of thought', uses the palette of the seasons to frame both nature's cycle and quiet self-reflection along the paths linking the two sites. Free, 10:30–17:00. One of the most scenic day trips on the Seoul commuter rail line.

title: Buan Red Sunset Festival
overview: The west coast at Byeonsan Beach turns crimson at dusk, and this three-day festival is built around that view: a red-wine festa and jazz festival against the sunset, a children's song contest, and a kite carnival of giant kites over the autumn sky. Sea breeze, music, wine, and the reddening horizon — aimed equally at families and couples. Free, 10:00–21:00, on the Byeonsan Peninsula's most famous beach.

title: NS Food Festa
overview: A food-culture festival at Harim's First Kitchen campus in Iksan, co-hosted by NS Home Shopping. Korea's largest amateur cooking competition anchors the program, joined by chef cooking shows, regional-produce tastings and sales, family performances — and the 'gourmet tour', a live look inside one of Korea's most advanced food-production facilities. Free, 10:00–17:00. A distinctly industrial-modern take on the Korean food festival.

title: Boeun Jujube Festival
overview: Boeun's jujubes were once royal tribute goods, and its 20th-anniversary festival is one of Korea's top farm-produce events — a three-time provincial best-festival winner. The riverside park at the foot of Songnisan National Park fills with jujube and produce markets (plus an online store and fresh-jujube call center for nationwide delivery), performances, and family programs. Free, 10:00–20:00. Pair it with Beopjusa Temple and Songnisan's autumn leaves for a full day.

title: Gangdong Prehistoric Culture Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Now celebrating its 30th edition, the Gangdong Prehistoric Culture Festival is the only festival in Seoul devoted to prehistoric culture. It highlights the historical importance of the Archaeological Site in Amsa-dong while giving visitors the chance to discover what life was like in prehistoric times through a wide range of programs. This year’s festival marks the 100th anniversary of the site’s discovery and takes place under the theme “The Breath of 6,000 Years, the Light of 100 Years, the Echoes of 30 Years.” The festival grounds are divided into four distinct zones inspired by water, fire, earth, and wind. Each zone brings its theme to life through creative displays, exhibitions, hands-on activities, nighttime programs, food, and performances. Over the course of three days, visitors can enjoy a unique experience that brings the past and present together.

title: Dongnaeeupseong History Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Dongnaeeupseong History Festival offers an immersive experience of the history and culture of Dongnaeeupseong Walled Town, where the Battle of Dongnaeseong Fortress took place against the Japanese army during the Imjin War in 1592. Highlights include a musical dramatizing the patriotic spirit of the Dongnae Governor during the battle and various hands-on experiences, such as participating as Dongnae citizens using traditional Joseon-era coins.
place: Areas of Dongnae Culture Center and Dongnaeeupseong Walled Town

title: Jeonggwan Eco-Stream Culture Festival
overview: A three-day community festival along the Jwagwangcheon — the garden stream running through Busan's Jeonggwan new town. Eco-stream experience programs put visitors in direct contact with the waterway's plants and wildlife, alongside sketching and writing contests, a parade, a family walking event, and performances and exhibitions that turn residents' daily riverside into a festival stage. Free, 10:00–20:00.

title: King Sejong & Chojeong Mineral Water Festival
overview: In 1444, King Sejong — creator of the Korean alphabet — spent 120 days at the Chojeong springs treating his ailments while continuing affairs of state. The festival celebrates that history at the restored Chojeong Haenggung (temporary palace), on the site of one of the world's three most famous naturally carbonated springs. Court reenactments, wellness programs, and hands-on booths fill the culture park. Free entry (some experiences paid), 10:00–21:00.
place: Chojeong Culture Park and Chojeong Haenggung

title: Royal Tombs of Joseon World Heritage Festival
overview: The UNESCO-listed royal tombs of the Joseon dynasty — 12 tomb clusters around Seoul and Gyeonggi, from Donggureung to Yeongwol's Jangneung — open up for ten days of tours, performances, exhibitions, and experience programs, each built on the particular story of its tomb. Now in its 7th year, the festival is the rare chance to see these serene, forested royal grounds animated after hours. Entry and program fees vary by site.
place: 12 Joseon royal tomb sites (Donggureung, Seooreung, Yungneung·Geolleung and others)
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: 2026 Chungnam Drone Festa
overview: A drone omnibus on the provincial-office plaza in Hongseong: a national drone competition of precision-piloting and search missions open to all comers, an industry conference, exhibition and piloting-experience zones — and the headliner, a light show of more than 1,200 drones animating the province's vision across the night sky. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Geumcheon Harmony Festival
overview: The Geumcheon Harmony Festival is Geumcheon-gu's representative festival, held annually for over 20 years since its inception in 2003. The festival aims to provide a venue for residents to rest, enjoy, and harmonize through the theme of music. Utilizing venues such as Geumnarae Jungang Park and the Plaza in front of the Geumcheon-gu Office, the event is planned to feature content that residents can enjoy and participate in. This includes a citizen-participatory show choir where residents come together to create beautiful melodies, exciting music performances, diverse experience booths, a sentimental flea market, and delicious food trucks.
place: Geumcheon-gu Office Palaze, Geumnarae Jungang Park

title: Gumi Food Festival
overview: Started in 2022 to lift spirits and small businesses after the pandemic, Gumi's food festival packs the Songjeong food street with some 200 menu items — one of the largest spreads on the Korean festival circuit — plus performances and children's content across all age groups. Free entry (some zones paid), 12:00–20:00 in the city center.

title: Siheung International Youth Festival (SIYF)
overview: Korea's largest youth-club festival: some 584 clubs and 7,800 teenagers from Siheung's youth-club support program plan and run the entire event themselves — performances, experiences, exhibitions, and exchange programs spanning volunteering, academics, sports, dance, bands, and the arts. International youth groups join through exchange partnerships, giving it a growing global dimension. Free, 13:00–21:00 at Siheung City Hall.

title: Gangneung Coffee Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Gangneung is as renowned for its delicious coffee as it is for its scenic coastline. Strolling along the cafe-lined beaches of Gangneung, visitors can experience a coffee aroma that rivals the sea breeze. Famous coffee manufacturers attend the Gangneung Coffee Festival and hold a tasting event. At the opening ceremony, 100 baristas hold a “100 People 100 Tastes” performance where they simultaneously brew hand-drip coffee. Visitors are welcome to taste 100 kinds of coffee at this special event. During the festival, competitions are held to select the No. 1 barista for each category, including latte art, hand drip, and roasting. Tourists can also visit cafés in Gangneung that are taking part in the festival and receive a stamp to get a prize. Coffee enthusiasts should not miss this opportunity.
place: Gangneung Coffee Street and throughout the city
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Gangwon State, Gangneung-si

title: Sacheon Air Show
overview: The largest air show in southern Korea, held at Sacheon Airfield in the city that hosts Korea's aerospace agency and KAI, the national aircraft maker. Four days of flight demonstrations (including the Black Eagles aerobatic team in past editions), an aerospace-and-defense industry exhibition, aircraft and military-equipment displays, experience flights, academic sessions, and competitions spanning public, business, and government audiences. Free, 09:00–17:00.
sponsor: ROK Air Force · Gyeongsangnam-do · Sacheon City · KAI

title: Chiaksan Hanwoo Beef Festival
overview: Wonju's beef festival, run by the local livestock cooperative around the premium Chiaksan hanwoo brand raised in the clean air below Chiaksan National Park. Tastings and discounted sales are the core draw, joined by regional-produce markets, family programs, and local performance stages. Free entry (beef paid), 11:00–21:00 — the 12th edition of a reliably delicious regional fixture.

title: 17th Art Gwangju International Art Fair
overview: The Honam region's largest international art fair, filling the Kimdaejung Convention Center with around 110 galleries from 12 countries across painting, sculpture, and media art. Special exhibitions — a masterpiece show, collector 'propose' show, and rising-star showcase — broaden it beyond a sales floor, connecting Gwangju's contemporary-art scene (home of Asia's leading biennale) with international galleries and collectors. On-site tickets from 15,000 won (online cheaper).
fee: Adults 15,000 won on site (10,000 online) · VIP and youth rates available

title: Incheon Film Week 2026
overview: A film festival reviving Incheon's identity as a cradle of early Korean cinema, under the theme 'we are each other's future'. Three days at CGV Incheon Yeonsu pair a curated slate of films about people running toward their futures with family-friendly side programs. Free; the detailed schedule posts on the festival website ahead of opening.

title: Gwangju Kimchi Festival
addr: 111 Naebang-ro, Seo-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Gwangju Kimchi Festival is Korea’s representative kimchi festival, offering a variety of kimchi products for purchase and the chance to taste various kimchi dishes. Highlights include the “Thousand People’s Table” featuring diverse kimchi cuisine, a competition to discover kimchi masters, and a kimchi experience school with a range of engaging programs.

title: Seogwipo Chilsimni Festival
overview: Seogwipo's signature citizens' festival, filling the old downtown and the Cheonjiyeon Waterfall area with a street parade — the centerpiece, joined by residents and community groups — plus multi-genre performances, busking, local-artist stages, food, and flea markets. 'Chilsimni' (seventy ri) is the poetic old measure of the town's reach, and the festival works as a walking tour of Seogwipo's harborfront identity. Free, 10:00–22:00.
place: Cheonjiyeon parking area and old downtown

title: Yeoncheon Job's Tears Festival
overview: Yeoncheon is Korea's home of yulmu (Job's tears), the nutty grain brewed into one of the country's favorite warm drinks, and its festival sells the harvest at the source — set, remarkably, on the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site where Acheulean hand-axes rewrote Asian archaeology. Farm sales, agricultural-culture experiences, exhibitions, performances, and country-market food give it an old-school rural fair feel. Free, 10:00–17:00.

title: Yeoju Ogoknaru Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Yeoju Ogok Naru Festival celebrates Yeoju’s agricultural products and traditional culture. The festival features a Naru Madang that recreates the market street ambiance around the old traditional quay, an Ogok (five-grain) Madang with various agricultural and specialty products on sale, and traditional activity programs. There is also a food market and a craft market for a festival area.

title: Tteokbokki Festival
overview: Korea's flagship festival for its favorite street food, hosted by Daegu's Buk-gu at the iM Bank Park stadium grounds — three days, tens of thousands of visitors, and tteokbokki from famous vendors nationwide. Beyond the food zone: main-stage concerts, the 'Tteok-Fe Night', spicy-red lucky draws, a finish-your-tteokbokki challenge, and even a dedicated inbound tour program for Taiwanese visitors. Free entry, 11:00–21:30. Come hungry, leave red-lipped.

title: Gimcheon Gimbap Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Gimcheon Gimbap Festival is a local cultural tourism festival held in Gimcheon, Gyeongsangbuk-do. Gimbap may not be one of the city’s best-known specialties, but the festival was inspired by a playful word association between Gimcheon and “Gimbap Cheonguk (gimbap heaven).” The festival brings residents and visitors together with a lively mix of gimbap-themed activities, exhibitions, performances, and games. Visitors can make and taste gimbap themselves, with performances and hands-on activity zones offering something fun for all ages.
place: Jikji Culture Park and Samyeongdaesa Park, Gimcheon

title: Seoul BBQ Festival
overview: K-BBQ gets its own urban festival at Nanji Campground on the Han River. The self-BBQ zone hands you ingredients and grills with no gear required; 'BBQ Masters' brings star chefs to the fire; and BBQ Village gathers famous restaurants worth queueing for — all run 'campnic' style, camping-meets-picnic. Regional produce, desserts, performances, and experience programs fill the rest of the grounds. Ticketed; 12:00–21:00.

title: Hongseong Global BBQ Festival
overview: The Hongseong Global BBQ Festival held in Hongseong, a city of aesthetics, is a festival where visitors can enjoy various barbecue cultures from home and abroad in one place. You can taste unique barbecue dishes based on Hongseong's livestock resources such as Hongseong hanu (Korean beef) and Hongseong handon (Korean pork), and there will also be cooking demonstrations by famous YouTubers and chefs. Various performances such as drone shows, busking performances, and other live music performances, as well as hands-on experiences, are prepared for family visitors, making it a festival that people of all ages can enjoy.

title: 13th 21st Century Human Values Forum
overview: A humanities forum in Andong — Korea's Confucian heartland — themed 'a shaken world, the things that do not change'. Three days of keynote lectures, scholar and citizen sessions, exhibitions, tours, and networking take on war and peace, memory and record, AI and technology, closing with the proclamation of the Andong Declaration. Around 5,000 participants join on site and online. Free, 10:00–20:00 (times vary by day).
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gyeongsangbuk-do · Andong City

title: Seongnam-dong Coffee Festival
overview: Ulsan's old downtown of Seongnam-dong — where mid-century tearooms once nurtured the industrial city's literary scene — hosts a citizen coffee festival run by the district's cafe owners and baristas. Hand-drip demonstrations, latte-art experiences, brewing contests, brand tastings, a national barista performance competition, live music, and food markets fill the culture street. Free, 10:00–20:00.

title: Yesan Apple Festival
overview: The 23rd Yesan apple festival moves to Yedang Lake, home of Korea's longest pedestrian suspension bridge, pairing the region's famous apples with its biggest landmark under the theme 'a sweet day at Yedangho'. Apple wine and desserts meet jazz, gugak, and classical crossover stages, while the two-day 'Apple Sale Festa' — run by the growers' cooperative — sells premium fruit at farm prices. Free, 10:00–20:00.

title: Goyang Haengju Hanwoo BBQ Festival
overview: Goyang's livestock cooperative throws a one-day charcoal-grill festival for Haengju hanwoo, the city's premium beef brand. Free tastings of charcoal-grilled beef anchor the event, with quality-controlled cuts sold direct from farms and family entertainment alongside — a compact, appetite-driven local festival rather than a sprawling production. Free, 10:00–17:00.
place: By Goyang Fire Station (Jugyo public lot)

title: Cheongsong Apple Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Cheongsong Apple Festival is held in autumn when the renowned Cheongsong apples, called a “masterpiece crafted by nature,” are at their peak. The festival celebrates the joy of a bountiful harvest, sharing the delicious taste and nutrition of Cheongsong apples through various enjoyable and educational activities.
place: Area of Yongjeoncheon Stream and Hyeonbiam Cliff

title: Jeju Olle Walking Festival
overview: The Jeju Olle Walking Festival is held every November, when Jeju's nature is at its finest. Participants walk the trails for three days while enjoying various cultural and artistic performances, traditional games, village programs, and Jeju cuisine. At times, concerts are held against the backdrop of the sound of waves, while at other times, traditional Jeju performances take place against the backdrop of the festival fields. Visitors can also enjoy food made with local agricultural and marine products that satisfy all five senses. With approximately 10,000 walkers participating annually , the Jeju Olle Trail Walking Festival is establishing itself as a global walking festival, with an increasing number of foreign participants from countries such as China, Taiwan, Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada each year.
fee: General 30,000 won / Discount 25,000 won (* Born 2008 or later)

title: Fisherman's Market X Port Village Tongyeong
overview: Tongyeong — Korea's seafood capital on the southern coast — pairs its fisherman's market with the Port Village food-festival brand for three days on the triathlon plaza. Booths build menus around the port's signature catch: oysters, eel, sea squirt, red seabream; performance booths cook live in front of you; and chef-consulting booths develop new dishes with name chefs. Free entry, 10:00–21:00, with the city's famous harbor food alleys minutes away.

title: Gimhae Buncheong Ceramics Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Gimhae Buncheong Ceramics Festival highlights the excellence of Buncheong ceramics and their everyday appeal. The festival offers a chance to see a wide variety of ceramics and participate in hands-on activities such as traditional kiln firing.
place: Area of Gimhae Buncheong Ceramics Museum and Clayarch Gimhae Museum
fee: Free (fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Busan Illustration Fair V.7
overview: The southern edition of Korea's leading illustration fair, run by the organizers of the Seoul Illustration Fair at BEXCO. Around 600 booths span illustration, painting, picture books, independent publishing, character design, graphics, games, animation, webtoons, and calligraphy, with popular Korean and international creators selling originals and goods directly. Adults 11,000 won (early bird 6,000); children free.
fee: Adults/teens 11,000 won · Early bird 6,000 won · Children free

title: Gumi Ramyun Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Gumi is home to Korea’s only downtown festival dedicated to ramyeon. Visitors can buy ramyeon fresh off the production line at Nongshim’s Gumi Factory and try a wide range of creative ramyeon dishes. The festival also offers themed exhibitions, hands-on activities, photo spots, stage performances, and various special events.

title: Hwasun Unjusa Culture Festival
overview: Unjusa is one of Korea's most enigmatic temples — the 'valley of a thousand Buddhas and a thousand pagodas', where carved stone figures and towers dot the hillsides and a giant reclining Buddha lies unfinished per its legend. The autumn festival fills the tranquil grounds with bell-ringing, pungmul percussion, multi-genre concerts, temple-wide mission games, and traditional culture programs. Free, 10:00–17:00 — worth the trip for the temple alone.

title: Brotherly Love Festival
overview: Yesan's Daeheung township is home to the beloved Korean folktale of two brothers who secretly carried rice sheaves to each other's fields by night — and this family festival retells it through storytelling programs, traditional games, family events, performances, and a local-food market at the Brotherly Love Park. The Yedang Lake suspension bridge and monorail are nearby for a full county day out. Free, 10:00–20:00.

title: Pohang International Fireworks Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Pohang International Fire & Light Festival is an internationally renowned event themed around the images of “light,” symbolizing the global steel city of Pohang, and “fire,” representing the hot blast furnaces. Performers and local citizens dress up in all sorts of costumes and masks to join in the Fire & Light Parade, which marks the colorful beginning of the festival. The festival culminates in the International Fireworks Show, the highlight of the evening. The world’s best teams participate in the festival every year to give a spectacular show of fireworks against the backdrop of Yeongilman Bay. The festival began in 2004 to commemorate Pohang Citizens Day with a fireworks show and has since become a beloved celebrated annual festival, showcasing the pride of Pohang to its citizens.◎ TipYou can see the fireworks from Yeongildae Beach and Songdo Beach. Although you can’t hear the music from the show, you can watch the fireworks show peacefully at a less crowded seashore. After the show, you can move to Hyeongsangang Sports Park, the festival venue, to enjoy the rest of the festival’s programs.
place: Hyeongsangang Sports Park and throughout Pohang

title: 20th Century Photography Masters: Light, Stopping Time
overview: Eighty original physical prints by 17 masters who built modern photography — Henri Cartier-Bresson, Tina Modotti, William Klein among them — drawn from the Gallery Lumiere collection. In an age of disposable digital images, the show insists on the weight of the analog print: silver-salt and platinum textures carrying the air and temperature of the moment the shutter fell. A meditative counterpoint to the scrolling feed, at Art Chosun Space near City Hall. Adults 12,000 won; 50% off on Culture Day.
fee: Adults 12,000 won · Youth/seniors 9,000 won · Infants free

title: Gyeonggi Rice Dessert Festa
overview: A dessert expo championing Gyeonggi rice as a baking ingredient: rice bakeries and rice-tteokbokki makers gather at Suwon Messe with sales zones, competitions, and hands-on programs promoting a healthier rice-based dessert culture. Free, 11:00–17:00 — a niche but tasty window into Korea's rice-flour baking boom.

title: Busan Bridge Marathon
overview: A winter road race through the marine city, gathering at BEXCO with two distances: a full marathon (entry requires a verified sub-4:30 finish from another race) and a 10km open to anyone 18 or older. The course shows off Busan's bridges and waterfront in the crisp December air. Full course 80,000 won, 10km 60,000 won; start 07:30.
sponsor: Busan Metropolitan City · Korea Athletics Federation · KNN

title: Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2026 festivals. Details for the 2027 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Held in Hwacheon, Gangwon-do, the Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival is a one-of-a-kind winter event that was named one of CNN's “Seven Wonders of Winter” in 2011. The festival takes place every January, when the famously pristine waters of Hwacheoncheon Stream freeze solid. Visitors can catch sancheoneo, mountain trout often called the "Queen of the Valley", through ice fishing or even with their bare hands. The freshly caught fish can be enjoyed immediately as raw slices or grilled on the spot. Beyond fishing, the festival features a wide range of winter attractions, including ice sledding, snow sledding, and bobsledding, drawing more than one million visitors each year.

title: Vegan & Halal Beauty Fair
overview: The Vegan & Halal Beauty Fair provides visitors an opportunity to explore beauty brands and products embodying diverse values ​​and standards, including vegan and halal, all in one place. In particular, it provides a special opportunity to encounter and experience new brands and products that are usually difficult to come by, as well as to discover changing beauty trends and the flow of new K-Beauty up close.
